### What

Modify `.claude/hooks/session-logger.sh` so each Claude session gets its own

1. llm-wiki/document-intelligence candidates,
2. existing/in-flight coverage,
3. code/vendor/internal exclusions,
4. private/project-sensitive exclusions, and
5. future source-family package candidates requiring separate approval.

- preserve the raw-data boundary: no copying/promoting raw content to git/wiki;
- classify discovered raw-like roots by source family, sensitivity, target wiki/domain, existing issue mapping, and recommended next action;
- update or define a durable metadata/routing artifact under the document-intelligence surface;
- link resulting source-family work back to vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#13, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2392, and vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2487;

issues.title: audit(security): verify branch/ruleset protections across public repos after collaborator-only lockdown
issues.body:
## Summary
Audit public repository rulesets, branch protection, issue/PR permissions, and contributor surfaces after the interaction-limit lockdown in #2546.

## Why
`collaborators_only` interaction limits reduce public issue/PR/comment noise, but they are temporary and do not replace branch protection / repository rulesets. We need a separate governance pass to ensure code and PR paths are protected consistently across public repos.

## Scope
For every active public `vamseeachanta/*` repo:
- Inventory default branch, branch protection, repository rulesets, required reviews, status checks, and force-push/delete settings.
- Inventory whether Issues, Discussions, Projects, Wiki, and Actions are enabled and whether each surface is intentional.
- Identify repos that should be archived, private, or have Issues disabled entirely.
- Recommend a minimum public-repo protection baseline for code/PR changes.
- Produce an evidence table and follow-up implementation plan; do not silently mutate branch protection without explicit approval because it can block active workflows.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Public repo table includes: visibility, archived state, default branch, interaction limit status, branch/ruleset status, Issues/PR surfaces.
- [ ] Findings separate already-hardened interaction limits from code-path protections.
- [ ] Recommended baseline distinguishes active Tier-1 repos from archived/static repos.
- [ ] Any proposed branch protection/ruleset changes are drafted as explicit plan-approved follow-up work.

## Related
- Root hardening: #2546

issues.title: feat(llm-wiki): plan metadata-only /mnt/ace-data raw-like source coverage triage
issues.body:
# feat(llm-wiki): plan metadata-only /mnt/ace-data raw-like source coverage triage

## Context
A user requested extending llm-wiki completion from raw data to llm-wiki completeness for `/mnt/ace-data/raw data`.

Live prerequisite checks found:
- `/mnt/ace-data` resolves to `/mnt/ace`.
- The exact literal path `/mnt/ace-data/raw data` does **not** exist.
- Metadata-only discovery found 14 raw-like directories under `/mnt/ace-data` (`raw`, `raw_data`, or `Raw`), with no raw content copied into git/wiki.
- Existing overlap must be preserved: vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#13 is the llm-wiki roadmap anchor, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2392 is the coverage-gap detector issue, and vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2487 already delivered the raw-data-to-readiness spine/control-plane.

## Problem
The raw-like mounted source estate is not yet consistently classified into:
1. llm-wiki/document-intelligence candidates,
2. existing/in-flight coverage,
3. code/vendor/internal exclusions,
4. private/project-sensitive exclusions, and
5. future source-family package candidates requiring separate approval.

Without this metadata-only triage layer, agents risk either missing high-value source families or over-promoting raw/private/project data into git/wiki.

## Metadata-only inventory evidence
Representative discovered raw-like directories:

| Source path | Metadata-only count | Initial routing |
|---|---:|---|
| `/mnt/ace-data/O&G-Standards/raw` | 28,803 files / 692 dirs | standards candidate, reconcile with vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#25/#2373/#2392/#2487 and completed bounded standards promotions |
| `/mnt/ace-data/client_projects/energy_bsee/raw_data` | 10 files | offshore/BSEE candidate; no direct duplicate issue found |
| `/mnt/ace-data/digitalmodel/docs/aqwa/data/scripts/mooring_analysis/raw` | 28 files | AQWA candidate; map to vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2103 rather than duplicate |
| `/mnt/ace-data/digitalmodel/docs/orcaflex/literature/examples/raw` | 38 files / 76 dirs | OrcaFlex examples candidate; map to vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2124 rather than duplicate |
| `/mnt/ace-data/frontierdeepwater/data/raw` | 4 files / 1 dir | offshore source candidate; no direct duplicate issue found |
| `/mnt/ace-data/worldenergydata/data/modules/hse/raw` | 97 files / 7 dirs | HSE/safety data candidate; no direct duplicate issue found |
| `/mnt/ace-data/docs/disciplines/misc/projects/0136_das/.../Data/Raw` | 215 files / 8 dirs | indexed as `acma-projects`/project-management gap; project-sensitive until separately approved |

Non-corpus/exclusion examples include empty `.gitkeep` raw dirs, Rust crate internals, Struts image assets, QGIS generated DXF output, SSI marketing images, OPM parser source internals, and similar code/vendor/generated/personal/project-sensitive surfaces.

## Scope
Create a canonical plan for a metadata-only raw-like source triage and routing artifact. The plan should:
- preserve the raw-data boundary: no copying/promoting raw content to git/wiki;
- classify discovered raw-like roots by source family, sensitivity, target wiki/domain, existing issue mapping, and recommended next action;
- update or define a durable metadata/routing artifact under the document-intelligence surface;
- link resulting source-family work back to vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#13, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2392, and vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2487;
- identify which families need separate follow-up issues before any summary promotion.

## Out of scope
- No raw data import into git/wiki.
- No direct llm-wiki page generation from raw documents in this issue.
- No standards content extraction from proprietary/copyrighted documents.
- No project-sensitive corpus promotion (SESA/Woodfibre/ACMA/DAS/client material) without separate explicit approval.
- No implementation before canonical plan review and user approval.

issues.title: META: rebind 3 llm-wiki plan-approved issues stuck on missing approval markers (#2368/#2124/#2125)
issues.body:
## Summary

Three llm-wiki issues at `status:plan-approved` (#2368, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2124, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2125) have been stuck since 2026-04-28 due to a missing/stale approval-binding state. Codex's 10-thread parallel-implementation lanes correctly refused to execute, and the gate has held for 5+ days without remediation. This META issue captures the rot so it can be cleaned up in one pass.

## Why

Per the vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2460 contract (memory: `project_issue_2460_approval_binding.md`), `status:plan-approved` GitHub label is necessary but not sufficient — execution requires a revision-bound approval marker at `.planning/plan-approved/<n>.md` that names the approved plan SHA + review artifact paths. Otherwise agents can't confirm WHICH version of the plan was approved.

This was specifically designed as a load-bearing user-in-loop gate (memory: `feedback_never_offer_to_self_label_plan_approved.md`) — agents must NOT self-approve by creating the marker themselves.

The gate is doing its job. But the cleanup hasn't happened, and three valuable llm-wiki improvements have been frozen.

## Per-issue state (verified 2026-05-03)

### vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#22 faceted portal pages for large LLM-wiki domains

- GH labels: `status:plan-approved,status:working,agent:codex` ✓
- `.planning/plan-approved/2368.md`: **MISSING**
- Local plan `docs/plans/2026-04-23-issue-2368-faceted-portal-pages.md`: blob `b391641688` — header says `Status: draft` (REGRESSED from v2)
- Approved revision per Codex's 2026-04-28 comment: SHA `1c01062d8` — header in that SHA says `Status: draft (v2 — addresses r1 findings)`, blob `b1df634b3`
- Codex blocker comment: 2026-04-28T09:17:06Z (3 retry passes, all gated)
- Likely cause of plan regression: `feedback_merge_race_silent_revert.md` pattern during auto-sync

**Remediation:**
```bash
git checkout 1c01062d8 -- docs/plans/2026-04-23-issue-2368-faceted-portal-pages.md
# Then create .planning/plan-approved/2368.md with marker:
#   plan_sha: 1c01062d8
#   plan_blob: b1df634b3943db8f99888cb120ccf9be6ce245fe
#   review_artifacts:
#     - scripts/review/results/2026-04-23-plan-2368-claude.md
#     - scripts/review/results/2026-04-23-plan-2368-codex.md
#     - scripts/review/results/2026-04-23-plan-2368-gemini.md
#   approved_by: vamseeachanta
#   approved_at: <ISO timestamp of human approval>
git add docs/plans/2026-04-23-issue-2368-faceted-portal-pages.md .planning/plan-approved/2368.md
git commit -m "markers(plan-approved): bind vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#22 to v2 SHA 1c01062d8"
```

### vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2124 extend ingestion to Orcina resources/examples/training

- GH labels: `status:plan-approved,status:working,agent:codex` ✓
- `.planning/plan-approved/2124.md`: **MISSING**
- Plan file: **MISSING** entirely (no `docs/plans/*2124*` exists)
- Codex blocker comment: 2026-04-28T09:18:13Z — also flags upstream dependency on vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2471 still being open
- Note: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2471 status as of 2026-05-03 (verify before remediating)

**Remediation:** plan needs to be authored or located before binding. May be that the plan was lost to the same merge-race that ate vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#22's v2 content.

### vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2125 auto-refresh ingestion on Orcina releases

- GH labels: `status:plan-approved,status:working,agent:codex` ✓
- `.planning/plan-approved/2125.md`: **MISSING**

**Remediation:** check if commit `e4b6193236` is salvageable; either land it or rebind plan + re-execute.

## Scope

This META issue is for **diagnosis + decision-making**, not implementation:

- Confirm the 3 issues' approval-binding state matches what's recorded above (re-verify before acting)
- For each: decide rebind / re-plan / archive / continue-as-is

## Acceptance

issues.title: fix(security): narrow #2552 external-contributor runbook tests + scenario 3 — drop privacy-leaking test, define ingestion vector, resolve interaction-limit contradiction
issues.body:
**Source:** #2552 plan-review queue audit 2026-05-03. Per [#2552 approval marker](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/blob/main/.planning/plan-approved/2552.md), the runbook content was approved despite a 4+ day Tier-D persistent-MAJOR pattern (claude/codex/gemini all MAJOR across 4+ rounds). The architectural defects under those MAJORs are deferred here for a focused fresh plan.

## Defects to address (from latest reviews)

### 1. Privacy-leaking test (Gemini, repeat)
The proposed `test_runbook_references_triggering_issues_without_personal_name` requires hardcoding the external commenter's PII into the test file to assert its absence. **Resolution:** drop the negative-presence assertion; only positively assert presence of issue numbers (#2401, #2546, #2550).

### 2. Undefined ingestion vector under `collaborators_only` lockdown (Gemini, repeat)
Plan tells operators to reply via `CONTRIBUTOR_INTEREST_TEMPLATE` but #2546's `collaborators_only` lockdown blocks the input channel. **Resolution:** explicitly define the ingestion vector (likely email or a designated public form) since GitHub interactions are blocked.

### 3. Security-posture contradiction in scenario 3 (Gemini, repeat)
Scenario 3 suggests "temporary lift of interaction limit" — globally undermines #2546's lockdown for one request. **Resolution:** either (a) drop scenario 3 entirely from in-scope work, or (b) define a per-user allowlist mechanism that doesn't lift the global limit.

### 4. Plan-internal contradictions (Claude, repeat)
- Untestable acceptance criteria (negative-presence checks for arbitrary unspecified strings)
- HTML-comment metadata contradicts surrounding table (plan was patched in layers without re-reading itself)

**Resolution:** restart from a clean T1 spec; do not iterate on the existing plan.

## Acceptance

- [ ] New plan filed under `docs/plans/` addressing items 1-4 explicitly
- [ ] Plan goes through one Claude+Gemini review cycle (Codex skipped per #2479 unless version-pin lands first)
- [ ] No regression on the runbook content already approved via #2552

## Severity

Medium — the runbook content is live (approved); this issue prevents drift between the runbook and its enforcement layer.

issues.title: fix(digitalmodel-tests): TestFiscalRegimeTaxAdjustment passes locally, fails in CI
issues.body:
## Symptom

`tests/field_development/test_economics.py::TestFiscalRegimeTaxAdjustment` (11 test items including parametrizations) passes locally but all 7 unparametrized methods fail in GitHub Actions CI.

## Evidence

**Local pass** — workspace-hub host (Linux, Python 3.11.14, default seed `--randomly-seed=1346970201`):
```
tests/field_development/test_economics.py::TestFiscalRegimeTaxAdjustment ...........  [100%]
============== 11 passed in 5.87s ==============
```

**CI fail** — `vamseeachanta/digitalmodel` GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04, Python 3.11.15:
```
tests/field_development/test_economics.py ......................................FFFFFFF
```
38 dots (`TestEconomics*` and earlier classes pass), then 7 F's (consecutive failures). Class boundaries match `TestFiscalRegimeTaxAdjustment` (file lines 989-1131).

CI run: [`25239910690`](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/actions/runs/25239910690)

## Investigation needed

The class was added in commit `8739183f feat(field-dev): apply fiscal regime tax adjustments to economics cashflows (#2050)`. Locally on the workspace-hub canonical host all tests pass. CI tests fail.

Possible causes:
- Python 3.11.14 vs 3.11.15 stdlib difference (decimal/float behavior in NPV calc)
- Locale/currency-formatting environment variable assumed by tests
- Random-seed sensitivity (`pytest-randomly` produces different orderings; CI seed unknown)
- Floating-point hardware divergence between runner CPU and developer CPU
- Environment env-var `FISCAL_REGIME_DEFAULT` or similar that's set locally but not in CI
- Timezone-dependent date arithmetic (CI runs in UTC)

The actual failure tracebacks were not surfaced by the Quality Gates `output_tail` JSON capture (truncated). Next investigator should:

1. Run a focused CI invocation with `pytest -v --tb=long tests/field_development/test_economics.py::TestFiscalRegimeTaxAdjustment` and capture full output
2. Compare environment between developer host and CI runner (`pip freeze`, `env | grep -E 'LOCALE|TZ|FISCAL'`, Python patch version)
3. If random-seed sensitivity: the class likely depends on test-ordering state leak from a fixture or module-level mutable

## Workaround in place

The class is currently skipped via `@pytest.mark.skip` with a reference to this issue. Once the root cause is identified and fixed, remove the skip decorator. Workaround landed in PR [vamseeachanta/digitalmodel#541](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/541).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Identify root cause of CI-vs-local divergence
- [ ] All 11 `TestFiscalRegimeTaxAdjustment` tests pass on CI
- [ ] Remove `@pytest.mark.skip` decorator from the class
- [ ] CI Quality Gates passes without this class skipped

## Provenance

This issue was filed concurrently with PR [vamseeachanta/digitalmodel#541](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/541) which unblocked the digitalmodel Quality Gates pipeline (workspace-hub [#2574](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2574)). The fiscal-regime test failure was masked by the earlier `seaborn`-import collection error and only became visible after the bulk infra fixes landed.

issues.title: feat(doc-intel): MCP server exposing doc_key lookup, wiki search, registry query
issues.body:
## Problem

Each AI agent in the ecosystem (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Hermes orchestrator) currently re-implements doc-intelligence access patterns:
- Claude Code: grep + `Read` + skill recall.
- Codex: limited — no filesystem access from sandbox (per `feedback_codex_needs_pushed_artifact.md`).
- Gemini: inconsistent; no unified lookup.
- Hermes: custom Python helpers in `scripts/orchestrator/hermes/`.

This causes:
1. Duplicated retrieval code across agents.
2. Codex cannot participate in retrieval-gated workflows (#2208) because it can't read `data/document-index/`.
3. No single point to measure retrieval quality or log queries.
4. #1804 is evaluating external MCP servers but nothing builds an *internal* MCP server for our own intelligence.

## Deliverable

An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server exposing read-only tools for the doc-intelligence ecosystem:

| Tool | Inputs | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `doc_key_lookup` | `doc_key` | registry entry, paths, provenance, status |
| `wiki_search` | query string, domain filter | top-K L3 page paths + excerpts |
| `registry_query` | YAML path filter, field filter | matching registry rows |
| `coverage_status` | discipline/domain | wiki-coverage metrics for that domain |
| `cfr_lookup` | Title, part/section | CFR registry entry + text (depends on CFR-ingestion issue) |

Transport: stdio MCP per standard; optional HTTP bridge for Hermes.
Location: `scripts/mcp/doc_intel_server/` (Python using `mcp` SDK).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] MCP server at `scripts/mcp/doc_intel_server/server.py` with `pyproject.toml` declaring it
- [ ] All 5 tools implemented with JSON-schema input validation
- [ ] Registered in Claude Code `.claude/mcp-servers/doc-intel.json`
- [ ] Registered in Gemini CLI config (`.gemini/mcp-servers.yaml` or equivalent)
- [ ] Hermes orchestrator can invoke via stdio or HTTP-bridge
- [ ] Rate-limited query logging to `logs/mcp/doc-intel/queries-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` for audit
- [ ] Test suite covers: tool schema validation, empty result handling, concurrent access
- [ ] Documentation at `docs/document-intelligence/mcp-server.md` (usage, tool reference, examples)
- [ ] No writes — server is read-only (enforced at tool level, tested)

## Dependencies

- Hard-depends on: embeddings-index issue (this bundle) — backs `wiki_search`
- Soft-depends on: retrieval-augmented-planner issue (this bundle) — shares the embeddings corpus
- Soft-depends on: CFR-ingestion issue (this bundle) — backs `cfr_lookup` (can be stub on first ship)
- Relates to: #1804 (MCP server evaluation) — this is the first internal MCP server and should inform the evaluation framework

## Notes

- Read-only by design: no promotion, no writes, no mutations. Write paths remain in existing scripts.
- Codex impact: per `feedback_codex_needs_pushed_artifact.md`, Codex sandbox blocks filesystem reads. The MCP server bridges this — Codex can invoke MCP tools to retrieve doc-intel without local FS access.
- Performance budget: <500ms p95 for `doc_key_lookup`; <2s p95 for `wiki_search` with embeddings backend.
- Security: server must not expose `.env`, `config/secrets/`, or any gitignored path; path allowlist enforced at tool layer.

## Deliverable

A nightly-refreshed embeddings index keyed by `doc_key` (per operating model §3) covering:
- All L2 registry entries with non-null summary or extracted content.
- All L3 wiki pages (`knowledge/wikis/*/wiki/**/*.md`) with content-addressable chunk IDs.

Storage: `data/document-index/embeddings.parquet` (or `.duckdb`) + `data/document-index/embeddings-manifest.yaml` (model name, version, refresh timestamp, row counts).

Query CLI: `uv run python scripts/knowledge/query_embeddings.py --text "..." --top-k 10 --layer L2|L3|both`.

- [ ] Model selection documented in `docs/document-intelligence/embeddings-model-selection.md` (spike deliverable; BGE-M3 / Voyage / `text-embedding-3-large` comparison)
- [ ] Unit tests cover: index build idempotency, query result stability, model-version gating

Issues with `status:plan-approved`, canonical plan, and committed `.planning/plan-approved/<issue>.md` marker; safe for overnight implementation waves.

High-value open issues without plan artifacts, ranked for the next planning-only batch.

- Day shift: requirements, PRD/issues, plan/review, QA.

Two patterns exist in `wikis/engineering/wiki/sources/`. The proposed page follows **Pattern B (external/community sources)**, matching the only existing precedent for an external-URL source (`2026-04-17-hn-cadquery.md`):
- `title` (string)
- `tags` (list)
- `sources` (scalar list of URLs)
- `added` (date)
- `last_updated` (date)
- `domain: engineering`

Pattern A (internal/repo-doc sources, e.g., `agent-equivalence-architecture-doc.md`) uses `source_path`, `source_type`, `ingested` — **not applicable here** because the source is an external GitHub repo, not a workspace-hub internal doc.

### Documents consulted
- Workflow memory `project_llm_wiki_external_post_ingest_workflow.md` — 8-step ingest pattern; firewall language pinned.
- Strategic-role memory `project_llm_wiki_strategic_role.md` — coverage gaps are first-class defects; routing principle.
- Spinout governance `project_llm_wiki_spunout.md` — confirms target repo + license firewall.
- Codex adversarial reviews at `scripts/review/results/2026-05-09-plan-2659-codex.md` (round 1, MAJOR) and `2026-05-09-plan-2659-codex-r2.md` (round 2, MAJOR — produced revision-3 corrections).

### Gaps identified
- No existing wiki page covers managed-agent orchestration patterns specifically (callable_agents API surface, handoff_request control plane, agent.yaml + leaf-worker subagents structure).
- Concept-page gap: `concepts/managed-agent-orchestration.md` — acknowledged but **deferred** per YAGNI.

## Files to Change

### 1. New source page

**Path:** `wikis/engineering/wiki/sources/2026-05-09-anthropics-financial-services.md`

**Slug rationale:** date-first `<YYYY-MM-DD>-<community>-<slug>` per Pattern B precedent (`2026-04-17-hn-cadquery.md`).

**Frontmatter (verbatim, Pattern B):**

```yaml
---
title: "Claude for Financial Services — managed-agent reference patterns (anthropics/financial-services)"
tags: [managed-agents, multi-agent-orchestration, plugin-architecture, anthropic, agent-handoff, leaf-worker-subagents]
sources:
  - https://github.com/anthropics/financial-services
added: 2026-05-09
last_updated: 2026-05-09
domain: engineering
---
```

No `license` or `observed_pushed_at` keys. License (Apache-2.0) and pushed_at observation cited in body prose (re-fetched at write time via `gh api repos/anthropics/financial-services --jq '.pushed_at'`).

**Section outline:**
- **Relevance** — Anthropic finance-vertical reference repo as methodology-grade input for marine/offshore wiki; agent architecture is domain-agnostic, finance is incidental.
- **Key teachings** — managed-agent cookbook structure (`agent.yaml` + `subagents/*.yaml` leaf workers + `steering-examples.json`); `callable_agents` research-preview pattern (depth-1 leaf workers); `handoff_request` events as cross-agent control plane (`scripts/orchestrate.py` reference loop); dual-surface principle; self-contained agent plugins; vertical-plugin decoupling; partner-built plugin pattern.
- **How this maps to existing wiki structure** — cross-links to `concepts/agent-delegation`, `concepts/orchestrator-worker-separation`, `concepts/multi-agent-parity`, `sources/agent-equivalence-architecture-doc`.
- **Use as a wiki source** — citation pointer for future managed-agent or plugin-architecture wiki content.
- **License and provenance** — Apache-2.0 per `LICENSE` file (verified GitHub MCP); pushed_at re-fetched at write time.

### 2. Index update — write-time counter rule

**Path:** `wikis/engineering/wiki/index.md`

**Pre-existing drift discovered during round-1 adversarial review:** at plan-draft time, frontmatter said `source_count: 16`, header said `## Sources (13 pages)`, actual file count was 23 (verified `gh api`). Both counters are deflated phantoms.

**Reconciliation rule (write-time-computed, NOT a frozen value):**

At write time, the implementing agent MUST execute this sequence:

```bash
# 1. Re-count actual sources/ files on llm-wiki main, immediately before staging the new page
N=$(gh api repos/vamseeachanta/llm-wiki/contents/wikis/engineering/wiki/sources \
      --jq '[.[] | select(.name | endswith(".md"))] | length')
TARGET=$((N + 1))

# 2. Read current index.md frontmatter source_count and header pluralization
# 3. Set frontmatter source_count = TARGET
# 4. Set header "## Sources (X pages)" → "## Sources (TARGET pages)"
# 5. Verify post-write: count files in sources/ (including the new one) equals TARGET
```

**At plan-draft time `N` was 23 → `TARGET` would be 24.** This frozen number is **a baseline expectation, not an acceptance criterion.** If `N` differs at write time (because another ingest landed first), the implementing agent uses the live `N`, not 23. The implementing agent MUST surface the divergence in the implementation comment if `N != 23`.

**Other diffs (NOT count-dependent):**
- Frontmatter `page_count: 107 → 108` (literal +1 for the new page; no drift here).
- Frontmatter `last_updated: 2026-05-06 → 2026-05-09`.
- Sources table: append row for new page (preserve existing ordering — verify at edit time).

**Rationale (reconcile-to-ground-truth, not literal +1):** marine-eng workflow memory's "+1-by-convention" applies to *inflated* phantoms (where literal +1 keeps the agreed offset). Engineering's phantoms are *deflated* — preserving deflation has no upstream-convention rationale and would compound an existing bug.

### 3. Log update

**Path:** `wikis/engineering/wiki/log.md`

**Append (firewall language pinned verbatim from `project_llm_wiki_external_post_ingest_workflow.md`):**

```markdown
## [2026-05-09] ingest | Anthropic — Claude for Financial Services

- Processed: https://github.com/anthropics/financial-services (Apache-2.0, observed pushed_at re-fetched at write time)
- Pages created: 1 — sources/2026-05-09-anthropics-financial-services.md
- Pages updated: 2 — index.md (page_count, source_count reconciled to ground-truth, last_updated, header pluralization, sources table row), log.md (this entry)
- Notes: Source-only ingest. No raw PDFs, private paths, vendor standards text, project specifications, clauses, tables, formulas, or source archive content copied. Index counter drift (deflated phantoms at plan-draft time: frontmatter source_count 16, header "13 pages", actual 23) reconciled to write-time ground-truth as part of this edit. Concept page on managed-agent orchestration deferred per YAGNI.
```

The literal phrase **"No raw PDFs, private paths, vendor standards text, project specifications, clauses, tables, formulas, or source archive content copied"** is the firewall-language verbatim string. Acceptance criterion checks for byte-equal match against this phrase.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New source page exists at `wikis/engineering/wiki/sources/2026-05-09-anthropics-financial-services.md` with frontmatter exactly matching the Pattern B block above (no `license`, no `observed_pushed_at` keys; `domain: engineering` present).
- [ ] All 4 cross-links resolve (verified post-write via `gh api`).
- [ ] **Counter rule satisfied (write-time-computed):** at write time, `N = count(wikis/engineering/wiki/sources/*.md before staging new page)`. Post-write `index.md` frontmatter must have `source_count: N+1`. Post-write `index.md` header must read `## Sources (N+1 pages)`. The implementation comment must record the observed `N` and resolved `N+1`. **Static value `24` is a baseline expectation only; the rule is the criterion.**
- [ ] `index.md` frontmatter: `page_count: 108` (literal +1, count-independent), `last_updated: 2026-05-09`.
- [ ] `index.md` sources table contains a row for the new page; row ordering preserves the existing convention.
- [ ] `log.md` ingest block appended; the literal phrase "No raw PDFs, private paths, vendor standards text, project specifications, clauses, tables, formulas, or source archive content copied" appears byte-equal in the Notes line.
- [ ] Single commit inside `llm-wiki/.git`, explicit-paths `git add` listing the three paths only (no `-A` / `.`), HEREDOC commit message, no `--amend`, no `--no-verify`.
- [ ] Pre-commit hooks pass naturally (no bypass).
- [ ] No workspace-hub issue refs in the commit body (firewall).
- [ ] Push deferred until separately authorized in a follow-up.

## Hermes Cleanup Mitigation (operationally specific)

**Detection trigger** at implement time:
```bash
pgrep -af 'git (rebase|stash push|commit|merge|reset|checkout)' | grep -v "$$"
```
If any output AND any process under `pgrep -af hermes` is also active, treat as cleanup-window risk.

**Branching behavior:**
- **Default path (Hermes idle):** commit on `main` of `vamseeachanta/llm-wiki`.
- **Fallback path (Hermes active at implement time):** commit on a short-lived branch `ingest/2026-05-09-anthropics-financial-services` inside the `llm-wiki/.git` worktree. Do NOT push. Surface the branch name to the user; merge decision is theirs.

**Approval-gate behavior unchanged:** the `status:plan-approved` label + `.planning/plan-approved/2659.md` marker are still required *before* any wiki edit, regardless of which branch the commit lands on.

**Push policy:** push deferred in both paths.

## Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Cross-link target rename between exploration and write | Re-verify with `gh api contents` at edit time; abort write if any of 4 targets missing |
| Index sources-table ordering convention misread | Read full table at edit time; preserve existing order discipline |
| Pre-existing counter drift compounds into more drift | **Resolved revision-2 + revision-3** — write-time-computed rule, not frozen integer |
| **Source-count drift between plan-draft and implementation** (e.g., another ingest lands first) | **Resolved revision-3** — counter rule is a write-time computation; baseline `24` is informational only |
| Pre-commit hook flags Apache-2.0 attribution as license-discipline issue | Synthesize methodology only; cite repo URL + license in body prose; no verbatim README copy. Apache-2.0 is permissive — flag is unlikely. |
| Parallel session lands on `engineering/wiki/index.md` between read and write | Re-read inside same edit transaction |
| Hermes cleanup loop reverts the commit | **Resolved revision-2** — explicit detection trigger + branch fallback (see Hermes Cleanup Mitigation section) |
| Slug convention deviation from peer date-first pattern | **Resolved revision-2** — slug now date-first per Pattern B precedent |
| Frontmatter schema deviation from peers | **Resolved revision-2** — frontmatter now verbatim Pattern B; no invented `license` / `observed_pushed_at` keys |
| Firewall-language verbatim claim unverifiable | **Resolved revision-2** — exact phrase pinned in plan; acceptance criterion checks byte-equal match |
| Anthropic repo `pushed_at` value drifts between exploration and write | **Resolved revision-2** — re-fetch via `gh api` at write time; cite the value observed at write time, not at plan-draft time |

## Adversarial Review Status

**T1-scoped single-provider review** per `feedback_always_adversarial_review_scale_depth.md` (review depth scales to scope, presence is non-negotiable).

- **Round 1 (2026-05-09):** Codex CLI 0.130.0 → MAJOR, 7 findings, 5 blockers. Artifact: `scripts/review/results/2026-05-09-plan-2659-codex.md`.
- **Round 2 (2026-05-09):** Codex CLI 0.130.0 → MAJOR, 7 findings RESOLVED + 1 new defect (stale-count). Artifact: `scripts/review/results/2026-05-09-plan-2659-codex-r2.md`.
- **Round 3 (this revision):** dispatching after revision-3 lands.

## Approval Gate

This issue is at `status:plan-review`. Per `issue-planning-mode` skill and CLAUDE.md planning-workflow rule, the implementing agent must NOT proceed until the user applies `status:plan-approved`.

**Approval will not be requested until Codex round-3 returns APPROVE or MINOR.**

To approve (after round-3 settles):
```bash
gh issue edit 2659 --repo vamseeachanta/workspace-hub \
  --remove-label "status:plan-review" --add-label "status:plan-approved"
mkdir -p .planning/plan-approved && echo "Approved by: $(git config user.name)" > .planning/plan-approved/2659.md
```

I will NOT self-approve, will NOT pre-authorize downstream agents in any handoff prompt, and will WAIT until both signals are present (label + marker) before any wiki edit.

issues.title: FEATURE: Tier-1 Repo Ecosystem Refactoring — audit, plan, execute with Claude Code plan mode
issues.body:
## Summary

Systematic refactoring of the workspace-hub repo ecosystem, starting with tier-1 repositories. The goal is to reduce architectural debt, consolidate duplicate patterns, enforce consistent structure, and improve agent navigability across all tier-1 repos.

## Tier-1 Repos (Priority Order)

| # | Repo | Purpose | Maturity | Depends On |
|---|------|---------|----------|------------|
| 1 | `digitalmodel/` | Engineering digital twin (asset integrity, CP, GIS, hydro) | beta | assetutilities |
| 2 | `assetutilities/` | Shared engineering utilities (config, units, calculations) | stable | — |
| 3 | `assethold/` | Asset portfolio financial analysis | beta | assetutilities |
| 4 | `worldenergydata/` | Global energy market data (BSEE, EIA, drilling) | beta | assetutilities |
| 5 | `CAD-DEVELOPMENTS/` | CAD solvers, models, database, utilities | beta | — |
| 6 | `aceengineer-website/` | Consulting website | — | — |
| 7 | `aceengineer-strategy/` | GTM, business strategy | — | — |
| 8 | `sabithaandkrishnaestates/` | SKEstates Inc. business ops | — | — |

## Refactoring Scope

### Phase 1: Audit (analysis-only, no code changes)
- [ ] Run `repo-architecture-analysis` on each tier-1 repo
- [ ] Identify cross-repo duplicate code (especially assetutilities consumers)
- [ ] Map dependency graph (imports, shared configs, data flows)
- [ ] Catalog test coverage per repo (current state)
- [ ] Identify orphaned/dead code, unused modules, oversized files (>400 lines)
- [ ] Score each repo against the Control-Plane Contract (AGENTS.md, provider adapters)
- [ ] Identify skill duplicates across repos (134 known from vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1720 audit)

### Phase 2: Plan (per-repo refactor plans)
- [ ] Generate refactor plan per tier-1 repo with estimated effort
- [ ] Prioritize by: business value × technical debt severity × dependency impact
- [ ] Identify breaking changes and migration paths
- [ ] Define test coverage targets (tier-1 = 85% per pytest.tier1.ini)

### Phase 3: Execute (TDD, incremental, per-repo)
- [ ] Execute refactors repo-by-repo following dependency order (assetutilities first)
- [ ] TDD mandatory — tests before implementation
- [ ] Each repo refactor as a separate sub-issue for tracking

## Execution Strategy: Claude Code Plan Mode (Cloud)

### Claude Code `--permission-mode plan` ("Ultraplan")

Claude Code v2.1.92 supports `--permission-mode plan` which restricts the agent to **read-only analysis and planning** — no file writes, no shell mutations. This is ideal for Phase 1 (Audit) and Phase 2 (Plan).

**Proposed execution:**

```bash
# Phase 1: Audit each tier-1 repo in plan mode (safe, read-only)
claude --permission-mode plan \
  --print \
  --model claude-opus-4-6 \
  --max-budget-usd 5 \
  -p "Audit the repository architecture of digitalmodel/. Analyze: module structure, dependency graph, test coverage, dead code, file sizes >400 lines, AGENTS.md compliance. Output a structured JSON report."

# Phase 2: Generate refactor plan
claude --permission-mode plan \
  --print \
  --model claude-opus-4-6 \
  --max-budget-usd 5 \
  -p "Given the audit report, generate a prioritized refactor plan for digitalmodel/. Include: breaking changes, migration steps, test targets, estimated effort per module."
```

### Cloud Execution Considerations

| Aspect | Status | Notes |
|--------|--------|-------|
| **Claude Code CLI** | Installed (v2.1.92) | Available on ace-linux-1 |
| **Plan mode** | Supported | `--permission-mode plan` — read-only, safe for audit |
| **API-key mode** | Supported | `--bare` + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for headless/cloud runs |
| **Print mode** | Supported | `-p` / `--print` for non-interactive batch execution |
| **Budget cap** | Supported | `--max-budget-usd` to control spend per run |
| **Cloud sandbox** | Possible | Can run via Hermes `delegate_task` with `acp_command='claude'` |
| **Max subscription** | Claude Max $200/mo | Rate-limited but sufficient for plan-mode audit |

### Recommended Approach
1. **Phase 1 + 2 (Audit + Plan)**: Run Claude Code in plan mode via `delegate_task(acp_command='claude')` — subagents get isolated context, read-only, budget-capped
2. **Phase 3 (Execute)**: Requires interactive Claude Code sessions with full permissions — NOT suited for autonomous cloud execution without user oversight

## Adversarial Review Requirements

Per [AI Review Routing Policy](docs/standards/AI_REVIEW_ROUTING_POLICY.md):

- **3-agent adversarial review at BOTH stages** (plan + code/artifact)
- Claude: orchestrator + reviewer
- Codex: implementation worker + adversarial reviewer
- Gemini: architecture reviewer + adversarial reviewer
- Max 3 review iterations per deliverable
- All MAJOR findings must be resolved before completion

### Review Checkpoints
1. **After Phase 1 (Audit)**: All 3 agents review the audit findings
2. **After Phase 2 (Plan)**: All 3 agents review each repo's refactor plan
3. **After Phase 3 (Execute)**: All 3 agents review code changes per repo

## Related Issues
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1567 — Feature: Continuous Repo Architecture Intelligence
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1545 — Agentic feature progression for repo ecosystem productivity under GSD
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1603 — Multi-repo architecture scan — expand scanner to all tier-1 repos
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1720 — Cross-agent session corpus audit (134 duplicate skills identified)
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1734 — chore: add domain skills to assethold (tier-1 with 0 skills)
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1661 — Architecture scanner: dependency cycle detection and layering violations
- vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#113 — ROADMAP: Repo ecosystem 3-6 month horizon

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Audit report generated for each tier-1 repo
- [ ] Refactor plan per repo reviewed and approved by all 3 agents
- [ ] Phase 3 sub-issues created with clear scope per repo
- [ ] Test coverage meets tier-1 target (85%) after refactoring
- [ ] Zero cross-repo duplicate skills remaining
- [ ] All repos score 100% on Control-Plane Contract compliance
- [ ] Dependency graph documented and validated

issues.title: epic(digitalmodel-ci): domain-divided CI architecture replacing maxfail-masking pattern
issues.body:
## Why now

This session surfaced that digitalmodel's QG suite has been chronically green-washed by \`maxfail=20\` masking 200+ pre-existing failures across 53 test files. The admin-merge-via-Quality-Gates-failure pattern (PRs [#541](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/541), [#544](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/544), [#549](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/549), [#550](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/550), [#551](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/551), [#553](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/553), [#568](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/568), [#569](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/569)) is now the default merge path — operationally fast but strategically corrosive: every PR carries the same 'gate trips on unrelated debt' justification.

Root cause: a single repo-wide \`pytest --maxfail=20\` invocation can't distinguish 'this PR introduced a regression in its own scope' from 'unrelated debt elsewhere in the repo.' Per-domain CI fixes both.

## Architecture

**14-15 test domains** (per [#2616](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2616) sweep + tests/ tree):

\`asset_integrity\`, \`citations\`, \`contracts\`, \`field_development\`, \`hydrodynamics-diffraction\`, \`hydrodynamics-passing-ship\`, \`infrastructure-core\`, \`marine-engineering\`, \`naval-architecture\`, \`orcaflex\`, \`orcaflex-solver\`, \`solver-smoke\`, \`specialized\`, \`structural\`, \`workflows\`, \`misc\`

Each domain becomes:
- a separate pytest job in a GH Actions matrix
- with its own \`--with\` dep list (so e.g. redis/psycopg2/motor only attach to \`infrastructure-core\`, not the whole CI)
- with its own conftest fixtures and skipif policies
- with the existing \`maxfail\` removed (per-domain failure counts stay bounded by domain size)

## Decisions locked (this session, vamseeachanta)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Domain owner | All domains owned by \`vamseeachanta\` (single owner; CODEOWNERS encodes this) |
| Aggregator gate policy | **All domains must pass** for merge (no informational-only mode) |
| Run cadence | **Touched-domains-only on PRs**; **full matrix nightly** (cron) |
| Deprecation policy | No test deletion or blanket-skip without AI-attested 'source X is gone, no other consumers' commit per \`feedback_attestation_enables_contradiction_detection\` |

## Sub-tasks

- [ ] **A** — Domain inventory PR (\`tests/DOMAINS.md\` mapping every test directory → domain → dep set; informs all subsequent PRs). Read-only repo analysis. \`digitalmodel\`.
- [ ] **B** — \`.claude/quality-gates.yaml\` refactor: one gate per domain with its own command + deps. Aggregator gate depends on all. Drops repo-wide \`maxfail\`. \`digitalmodel\`.
- [ ] **C** — GH Actions matrix workflow: \`.github/workflows/quality-gates-by-domain.yml\` with \`strategy.matrix.domain\` for parallel runs + aggregator job. \`digitalmodel\`.
- [ ] **D** — Touched-domain detection: PR-time job that diffs changed paths against \`tests/DOMAINS.md\` and emits the matrix subset to run. Nightly cron uses full matrix. \`digitalmodel\`.
- [ ] **E** — Per-domain conftest extraction: move shared fixtures/skipifs from \`tests/conftest.py\` into each domain's local conftest. ~1 PR per domain (small each). \`digitalmodel\`.
- [ ] **F** — CODEOWNERS file with \`vamseeachanta\` as default owner. \`digitalmodel\`.
- [ ] **G** — Update workspace-hub agents.md + CLAUDE.md to encode the 'always test by domain during development' rule for AI agents. \`workspace-hub\`.

## After A-G land, the deferred cluster work re-routes by domain

| Cluster | Issue | New domain home |
|---|---|---|
| A — sys.modules pollution | [#2623](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2623) | \`contracts\` domain |
| D — infrastructure dep wall | [#2624](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2624) | \`infrastructure-core\` domain — its own \`--with redis --with psycopg2-binary --with motor\` |
| E — marine-engineering regressions | [#2625](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2625) | \`marine-engineering\` domain — its own targeted suite |

These clusters become much cheaper to fix per-domain than under repo-wide CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Domain inventory exists and is reviewable
- [ ] PR for trivial change (e.g. docs typo) only runs domains that own changed paths; runs in <2 min
- [ ] PR that touches multiple domains runs all touched domains; aggregator gates correctly
- [ ] Nightly full matrix runs all domains; failure surfaces per-domain in GH Actions UI
- [ ] No test files deleted as part of this work; debt that surfaces is filed per-domain for owner triage
- [ ] Existing admin-merge cycle ends — next post-A-G PR merges through the new gate without override

## Related

- [#2614](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2614), [#2616](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2616) — investigations that surfaced the masking
- [#2129](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2129) — issue-state drift / quality-gates audit umbrella
- [vamseeachanta/digitalmodel#543](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/543) — PR that introduced \`maxfail=20\`
issues.display_title: epic(digitalmodel-ci): domain-divided CI architecture replacing maxfail-masking pattern

- Post or prepare a verification report referencing #2546.
- Register the job in `config/scheduled-tasks/schedule-tasks.yaml` with a cadence safely before expiry, e.g. every 150 days / quarterly equivalent supported by the scheduler.

issues.title: fix(digitalmodel): test_packaged_yaml_in_built_distribution_preserves_existing_package_data flaky under parallel pytest sessions
issues.body:
**Discovered during:** #2603 implementation session on 2026-05-03; cross-ref [digitalmodel#548](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/548) post-merge verification.

## Problem

`tests/naval_architecture/test_rudder_stock_torque_sweep.py::test_packaged_yaml_in_built_distribution_preserves_existing_package_data` fails intermittently when run alongside other pytest sessions on the same host:

```
E     error: [Errno 2] No such file or directory
E     ERROR Backend subprocess exited when trying to invoke build_wheel
```

## Root cause

The test runs `uv run --no-sync --with build --with setuptools --with wheel python -m build --wheel --no-isolation --outdir <tmp_path>`. With `--no-isolation`, the build subprocess interacts with the project's tmp/build state. When two pytest sessions run concurrently against the same workspace (e.g., the `/whats-next` parallel verification pattern), the build subprocess can race against another session's tmp cleanup and hit ENOENT.

## Verification

Reproduced 2026-05-03:
- Run alongside `test_yaw_moment_sweep.py`: FAIL with ENOENT
- Run in isolation immediately after: PASS in 33-110s
- Re-run alongside other test, isolation-mode rerun: PASS

The flake is **not** caused by [digitalmodel#548](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/548) (#2603 fix). Verified by stashing the __init__.py diff: test still passed in isolation; flake was tmpdir-race-driven.

## Fix options (pick one)

- [ ] (a) Add `pytest.mark.filterwarnings`/`pytest_xdist_group` so this test runs in its own group, blocking parallel sibling tests
- [ ] (b) Switch to `--isolation` (full PEP 517 build env per invocation) — slower but no shared state
- [ ] (c) Add a retry decorator (`@pytest.mark.flaky(reruns=2)`) — accepts the flake as-is
- [ ] (d) Use a per-test scratch dir with `tmp_path_factory` and ensure no shared parent tmpdir

Recommended: (b) for correctness, (a) or (d) if (b) is too slow.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Test passes 10/10 under parallel-session contention (target host: ace-linux-1)
- [ ] No regression in solo-run timing > 50%

## Severity

Low — does not affect correctness of #2564/#2565/#2603 work; test is real and useful, just flaky under load.

```
    import yaml
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'
error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub.git'
```

## Root cause

`.git/hooks/pre-push` invokes `uv run --no-project python "$CONFIG_DRIFT_SCRIPT"` (line 132). The `--no-project` flag bypasses the worktree's local `pyproject.toml` and uses uv's ephemeral cache, which does NOT have `pyyaml` installed.

The system `python3` (miniforge in this user's setup) DOES have pyyaml, but the hook explicitly bypasses it via `uv run --no-project`.

## Reproduces on

- Any git worktree created via `git worktree add /tmp/<path>` whose new tree doesn't have a populated `.venv`
- Verified 2026-05-02 (`/tmp/agent-wt`, `/tmp/agent-wt2`) and 2026-05-03 (`/tmp/agent-wt4`)

## Workaround currently used

`PATH=/home/vamsee/miniforge3/bin:$PATH git push` — does NOT work (uv bypasses PATH for python resolution).
`git push --no-verify` — works, allowed by Iron Law for preservation pushes per `.claude/memory/topics/feedback_pre_push_hook_no_verify_for_preservation.md`. **Used twice in the last 24 hours.**

## Fix options

- [ ] (a) Change `uv run --no-project` to `uv run --with pyyaml` — declares the dep inline
- [ ] (b) Replace `import yaml` in `check_config_drift.py` with `tomllib` (stdlib, Python 3.11+) if the config files are TOML-compatible
- [ ] (c) Use `uv run` (without `--no-project`) so it picks up the worktree's `pyproject.toml`
- [ ] (d) Pre-install pyyaml in uv's tool cache via `uv tool install pyyaml`

Recommended: (a) — minimal diff, explicit, robust to worktrees.

## Affected scripts

`grep -rn 'uv run --no-project' .git/hooks/ scripts/quality/`:
- `.git/hooks/pre-push:132` — config drift check
- `.git/hooks/pre-push:203,221,239,255,258` — other ratchets
- `scripts/quality/check-all.sh:178,189,199,335,410,506,520,548,565,591` — multiple

If any of those import yaml/other libs, they'll have the same flaw. Audit recommended.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `git push` from a fresh `git worktree add` succeeds without `--no-verify`
- [ ] No regression in main-worktree pushes
- [ ] All `uv run --no-project` invocations in hooks + check-all.sh either use `--with <pkg>` or import only stdlib

## Severity

Medium — currently masked by `--no-verify`, but undermines the gate's purpose. Iron Law allows push --no-verify only for preservation; chronic use erodes the audit trail.

issues.title: feat(workstations): add reusable Hermes preflight readiness checker
issues.body:
## Summary

Build a reusable workstation preflight checker for Hermes-led cross-machine dispatch. The checker should turn the manual `ace-linux-2` probe from #2519/#2520 into a repeatable command that verifies host reachability, login-shell tool visibility, provider runtime readiness, GitHub auth state, repo cleanliness, and engineering-tool smoke readiness before work is assigned.

## Motivation

#2519 established that `ace-linux-2` can run Hermes/Codex only through a login shell and that `gh` auth can independently be invalid. This needs to become an automated gate so future workstations are not delegated work based on stale or partial assumptions.

## Scope

- Add a script/CLI entrypoint for workstation preflight checks.
- Support at least `ace-linux-1` local mode and `ace-linux-2` remote mode.
- Use login-shell checks for remote machines where user-level tools live under `~/.local/bin` or `~/.npm-global/bin`.
- Check and redact-sensitive-report:
  - hostname / reachability / canonical workspace path,
  - git repo branch/status/ahead-behind for tier-1 repos,
  - `gh auth status` and `gh api user` success/failure without token values,
  - Hermes provider/model config without secrets,
  - `codex`, `claude`, `gemini` command availability/version,
  - selected engineering tool presence/smoke checks.
- Emit both JSON and markdown reports under `docs/reports/` or a configured artifacts directory.
- Return non-zero only for clearly blocking failures; classify warnings vs blockers.

## Acceptance criteria

- A documented command can run the preflight against `ace-linux-2` via:
  `ssh ace-linux-2 'bash -lc "<probe>"'` or equivalent.
- Output never includes token/auth file contents.
- The current `ace-linux-2` `gh` auth failure is represented as a GitHub-mutation blocker, not as a total machine failure.
- Tests cover parsing/classification for at least reachable, auth-invalid, tool-missing, and clean-repo cases.
- The #2519 handoff/prompts can reference this checker instead of embedding ad hoc shell snippets.

## Related

- Parent: #2519
- Blocker/auth repair: #2520
- Committed baseline report: `docs/reports/2026-04-27-issue-2519-ace-linux-2-readiness-probe.md`

issues.body:
## Summary

Review and revise the mission/objective statements across all active workspace repos so future GitHub issue work can quickly answer:

1. what is this repo for?
2. what work belongs here?
3. what work should route elsewhere?
4. is the repo active, support-only, client/archive, or deprecated/no-new-issues?

This is the portfolio-wide complement to the Tier-1 routing/indexing work already tracked under vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2460-#2465.

## Why

The Tier-1 contract now improves code placement and routing, but the portfolio still needs a canonical mission/objective layer across all active repos. Without that layer, agents can still mis-route issues between overlapping repos such as:

- `workspace-hub` vs per-repo execution docs
- `assetutilities` vs repo-specific utilities
- `digitalmodel` vs client/project verticals
- `investments` vs `assethold`
- `client_projects` vs client-specific repos
- active engineering repos vs archives/reference repos

## Initial repo scope

Use `docs/BUSINESS_BRAIN.md` and live immediate-child git repos as the starting inventory.

### Tier-1

- `workspace-hub`
- `digitalmodel`
- `assetutilities`
- `aceengineer-website`

### Tier-2

- `OGManufacturing`
- `acma-projects`
- `frontierdeepwater`
- `seanation`
- `worldenergydata`
- `investments`
- `rock-oil-field`

### Tier-3 / support / archive candidates

- `aceengineer-admin`
- `aceengineer-strategy`
- `achantas-data`
- `achantas-media`
- `assethold`
- `client_projects`
- `doris`
- `hobbies`
- `pdf-large-reader` if present/active
- `sabithaandkrishnaestates`
- `saipem`
- `sd-work`
- `teamresumes`
- `CAD-DEVELOPMENTS` if confirmed active in this workspace

## Deliverables

1. Canonical portfolio mission/objective artifact, preferably `docs/REPO_MISSION_PORTFOLIO.md` or an equivalent linked from `docs/BUSINESS_BRAIN.md`.
2. Per-repo classification:
   - active product/library
   - client vertical
   - business/admin support
   - archive/reference
   - deprecated / no-new-issues
3. Per-repo mission/objective statement grounded in the strongest available source:
   - `.agent-os/product/mission.md`
   - `README.md`
   - `AGENTS.md`
   - `docs/README.md`
   - existing workspace-hub portfolio docs
4. Per-repo routing rule:
   - "work belongs here when..."
   - "work should route elsewhere when..."
5. Conflict/dedupe notes for overlapping repo missions.
6. Update links from `docs/BUSINESS_BRAIN.md` and/or `docs/ROUTING_INDEX.md` so the mission artifact is discoverable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every active repo in `docs/BUSINESS_BRAIN.md` has a current mission/objective row.
- [ ] Every immediate-child local git repo not listed in `docs/BUSINESS_BRAIN.md` is either added, explicitly excluded, or marked as inventory drift.
- [ ] Each row has a source path proving where the mission came from.
- [ ] Each row has an activity/status classification.
- [ ] Each row has an issue-routing rule for work that belongs vs work that should route elsewhere.
- [ ] Overlapping missions are explicitly called out and resolved or marked for follow-up.
- [ ] Tier-1 mission/objective rows are consistent with vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2460 and its child routing issues (#2461-#2465).
- [ ] The artifact is linked from a canonical workspace discovery surface.
- [ ] The plan receives adversarial review before implementation.

## Suggested execution waves

1. Wave 1: Tier-1 mission alignment and consistency with vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2460-#2465.
2. Wave 2: Tier-2 repo mission/objective review.
3. Wave 3: Tier-3/support/archive classification and no-new-issues guidance.
4. Wave 4: final portfolio table integration, dedupe/conflict notes, and discoverability links.

## Related

- Parent/umbrella: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1962
- Tier-1 structure epic: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2397
- LLM-wiki roadmap context: vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#13

Follow the normal issue gate:

Issue → resource intelligence → canonical plan in `docs/plans/` → adversarial plan review → `status:plan-review` → user approval → `status:plan-approved` → implementation.

issues.title: Set up Telegram mobile access for Hermes AI control
issues.body:
## Summary
Set up Telegram-based mobile access to Hermes/AI so Vamsee can interact with the agent, approve/adjust plans, tweak task lists, and monitor/steer work while on the move.

## Current user state
- Vamsee has logged into Telegram on the mobile device using phone/name.
- Next user-side action is to create a Telegram bot via `@BotFather`; the bot token must be handled as a secret and must not be pasted into public issue comments or chat logs.

## Recommended architecture
Use a Telegram **bot** connected to the Hermes gateway on `ace-linux-1`, not a separate human Telegram account for the AI.

Rationale:
- Telegram bots are the normal integration surface for programmatic message handling.
- Bot token can be stored in `~/.hermes/.env` and loaded by the gateway service.
- Access can be restricted to Vamsee's user/chat ID.
- Hermes gateway already supports Telegram and can run as a persistent service.

## Scope

### Phase 1 — Private single-user Telegram bot
- Create bot using `@BotFather`.
- Securely store bot token in `~/.hermes/.env` or password manager.
- Configure Hermes gateway Telegram integration.
- Restrict access to Vamsee's Telegram user/chat ID.
- Start gateway as persistent service on `ace-linux-1`.
- Verify mobile command/response loop.

### Phase 2 — Mobile operating guardrails
- Keep approval mode `manual` or `smart`; do not use approval `off` for mobile operation.
- Enable only mobile-appropriate toolsets initially.
- Confirm secrets are never transmitted through Telegram.
- Document restart/stop/status commands.
- Create quick-reference command sheet for on-the-move tweaks.

### Phase 3 — Optional enhancements after stable
- Voice-message STT/TTS for hands-free operation.
- Dedicated group/topic if DMs become cluttered.
- Additional user allowlist if needed.

## Task list
- [ ] Create Telegram bot with `@BotFather` from Vamsee's phone.
- [ ] Capture bot username and token securely; do not paste token into GitHub or chat.
- [ ] Configure Hermes gateway Telegram platform with `hermes gateway setup` or config edit.
- [ ] Add Telegram token to `~/.hermes/.env` and verify service can read it.
- [ ] Configure allowed users/chats to Vamsee only for initial rollout.
- [ ] Enable appropriate toolsets for mobile use: memory, session_search, cronjob, send_message, file, terminal, browser/web only as needed.
- [ ] Install/start gateway persistently: `sudo $(which hermes) gateway install --system`, then start/status.
- [ ] If systemd cannot see env vars, add `EnvironmentFile=/home/vamsee/.hermes/.env` to the service and restart.
- [ ] Test `/help`, `/status`, a simple task tweak, and a safe approval-gated action from mobile.
- [ ] Write a concise mobile command sheet for status checks, plan approvals, task-list updates, pause/kill commands, and GitHub-link requests.
- [ ] Optional: configure/test STT/TTS with one short voice note.

## Acceptance criteria
- Telegram bot responds to Vamsee from mobile through Hermes gateway.
- Unauthorized users/chats are blocked or ignored.
- Gateway survives shell logout/reboot via systemd or documented equivalent.
- Bot token is stored only in secret/config surfaces, not committed or posted.
- Mobile workflow supports: ask status, tweak a task list, request a GitHub link, and approve/revise/hold a plan.
- Quick-reference command sheet exists in a durable repo/docs location.

## Security / operations notes
- Do not paste the bot token into this issue.
- Prefer single-user allowlist for the first rollout.
- Keep mobile destructive actions approval-gated.
- Avoid approval mode `off` unless explicitly approved for a bounded test.
- Check gateway logs at `~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log` for troubleshooting.

## Suggested labels
`enhancement`, `cat:ai-orchestration`, `cat:operations`, `domain:integrations`, `domain:notification`, `priority:high`, `status:pending`

issues.title: fix(digitalmodel-ci): Quality Gates blocked by missing `seaborn` and hardcoded absolute paths
issues.body:
## Symptoms

Every digitalmodel PR currently fails the **Run Quality Gates** required check at the `tests` gate. Two open PRs hit the identical failure:

- [#540](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/540) — `docs(naval): point B1528 SIROCCO outputs to acma-projects` (docs-only, anchor values unchanged)
- [#539](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/539) — `docs(routing): add repo-wide operator map and registry`

Failure manifest (run `25230726625` for #540, run `25032587245` for #539):

```
Tests: 0 passed, 0 failed, 10 errors
stopping after 10 failures
```

## Root cause 1 — \`seaborn\` import not satisfied in CI

`src/digitalmodel/marine_ops/marine_analysis/environmental_loading/ocimf.py:27` does an unconditional `import seaborn as sns`. The `marine_ops/marine_analysis/__init__.py:73` chain transitively imports `ocimf` via `profiling.profile_modules:56`. Any test that imports anything under `marine_ops/marine_analysis` therefore fails collection with:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'seaborn'
```

This blocks at least 9 of the 10 CI-collection errors:

```
tests/hydrodynamics/aqwa/test_viscous_damping_determination.py
tests/marine_ops/marine_analysis/test_rao_quality_checks.py
tests/marine_ops/marine_engineering/catenary/test_catenary_integration.py
tests/marine_ops/marine_engineering/catenary/test_catenary_perf.py
tests/marine_ops/marine_engineering/catenary/test_run_quick.py
tests/marine_ops/marine_engineering/catenary/test_simplified.py
tests/marine_ops/marine_engineering/environmental_loading/test_ocimf.py
tests/marine_ops/marine_engineering/integration/test_end_to_end_workflow.py
tests/marine_ops/marine_engineering/integration/test_hydro_rao_integration.py
```

`seaborn` is currently declared only in the optional viz extra:

```toml
# pyproject.toml:182
viz = ["dash>=3.1.0,<4.0.0", "kaleido>=0.2.0,<1.0.0", "seaborn>=0.13.0,<1.0.0"]
```

CI does not install `[viz]`, so the unconditional import in `ocimf.py` always fails.

## Root cause 2 — \`/mnt/local-analysis/...\` absolute paths in tests

`tests/marine_ops/installation/test_go_no_go.py:15-16` hardcodes a developer's local workspace path:

```python
gng = load_module("go_no_go", "/mnt/local-analysis/workspace-hub/digitalmodel/src/digitalmodel/marine_ops/installation/go_no_go.py")
jl  = load_module("jumper_lift", "/mnt/local-analysis/workspace-hub/digitalmodel/src/digitalmodel/marine_ops/installation/jumper_lift.py")
```

CI runs at `/home/runner/work/digitalmodel/digitalmodel/` so the path resolves to nothing and pytest fails with `FileNotFoundError`.

The same anti-pattern is widespread in test data YAMLs:

```
tests/asset_integrity/test_data/API579/app_API579_12in_oil_cml28_b314.yml:77,79,84,85
tests/asset_integrity/test_data/API579/app_API579_12in_oil_cml31_b314.yml:77,79,84,85
tests/asset_integrity/test_data/API579/app_API579_16in_gas_b318.yml:77,79
... (additional matches likely; full grep needed)
```

This violates `.claude/rules/coding-style.md`:

> In scripts: use relative paths or `$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` / `${REPO_ROOT}` — never hardcode absolute paths (enforced: `scripts/enforcement/check-no-abs-paths.sh`)

The enforcement script presumably did not catch these because they live in test data YAMLs, not in shell/Python source. The check needs broadening, or these files need exempting and/or templating.

## Proposed fix scope

### Fix 1 — \`seaborn\` import

Two viable options; prefer (a) for least churn:

(a) **Make the `seaborn` import lazy** in `ocimf.py` — wrap visualization functions that actually use `sns` in a guarded import:

```python
def _make_chart(...):
    import seaborn as sns  # lazy: only required for viz output, not for module import
    ...
```

(b) **Promote `seaborn` to a base dependency** in `pyproject.toml` and remove the unconditional top-level import. Heavier — pulls `matplotlib` + `seaborn` into every install.

### Fix 2 — Absolute-path purge

1. Convert `tests/marine_ops/installation/test_go_no_go.py:15-16` to use a relative-path pattern (e.g., `Path(__file__).parents[3] / "src/digitalmodel/marine_ops/installation/go_no_go.py"`).

issues.title: chore(ci-health): digitalmodel Quality Gates coverage gate blocker (split from #2441)
issues.body:
## Context

Surfaced during #2441 implementation as out-of-scope per plan §Risks.

After #2441 added \`pylife\` dependency, the \`Quality Gates\` workflow's \`tests\` gate now passes (245 tests collect cleanly, 0 errors). However, the workflow may stay red overall because of a **separate** coverage-gate blocker.

## Problem

\`digitalmodel/src/digitalmodel/workflows/automation/quality_gates.py:285-295\` — \`_execute_coverage_gate\` returns \`GateStatus.ERROR\` when \`coverage.json\` is missing.

\`digitalmodel/.claude/quality-gates.yaml:10\` — \`tests\` gate command runs plain \`python -m pytest\` with **no \`--cov\` flag**, so \`coverage.json\` is never generated.

\`digitalmodel/.claude/quality-gates.yaml:100\` — \`ci_cd.strict_mode: true\` causes the coverage-gate ERROR to fail the overall workflow.

Net result: even with #2441's pylife fix landing, Quality Gates may continue to report failure because the coverage gate is structurally unable to succeed with the current configuration.

## Two candidate fixes

1. **Add \`--cov=src --cov-report=json\` to the tests-gate command** in \`.claude/quality-gates.yaml:10\` so \`coverage.json\` exists for the coverage gate to inspect. Aligns with the existing \`pyproject.toml\` config which already declares \`--cov=src\` under \`[tool.pytest.ini_options]\`.

2. **Make coverage gate optional** by setting \`ci_cd.strict_mode: false\` for the coverage gate specifically, OR removing the coverage gate from the strict gate list, OR adding a default \`coverage.json\` skeleton that satisfies the existence check without requiring real coverage data.

## Verification

After fix:
- \`gh run watch <next Quality Gates run> --repo vamseeachanta/digitalmodel\` — both \`tests\` and \`coverage\` gates pass
- \`gh run list --repo vamseeachanta/digitalmodel --workflow \"Quality Gates\" --branch main --status success --limit 1\` returns at least one run

## Source

Code review of #2441 plan §Deliverable + §Risks. Spotted by static inspection of \`quality_gates.py:285-295\` and \`.claude/quality-gates.yaml:10/100\`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Quality Gates workflow passes overall (both tests + coverage gates green)
- [ ] Coverage gate failure mode is either resolved (Option 1) or made non-strict (Option 2)
- [ ] Plan written + adversarial review + user approval before implementation per workspace planning workflow

Parent: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2424 (cross-repo CI audit)
Sibling: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2441 (CLOSED — pylife fix; surfaced this follow-up)

issues.title: digitalmodel: CadQuery spike for parametric offshore geometry generation
issues.body:
## Context

CadQuery is a Python library for parametric 3D CAD on the OpenCASCADE B-rep kernel. STEP export is high-fidelity, so downstream meshers (gmsh, Salome) can control density without being trapped by authoring-time facets — a good shape for offshore component geometry that feeds AQWA.

Discovered via HN discussion 2026-04-17 (180 points, 47 comments): https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47772725

> **Revised 2026-04-17 per [adversarial review](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2327#issuecomment-4269065194)**: time-boxed; scope narrowed to one family and one pipeline; go/no-go criteria quantified; LLM-codegen question dropped (covered by #2328); current-state baseline required in plan.

## Scope

**Time-box:** 4 hours of hands-on work. Stop and report at the cap regardless of completeness.

**Target pipeline (committed):** STEP (CadQuery) → gmsh → AQWA `QPPL DIFF` panel diffraction. Chosen because panel diffraction has the tightest mesh-quality requirements (hardest pipeline test); digitalmodel already consumes AQWA downstream; OrcaFlex line-element path is a trivial follow-up if this works.

**Target family (committed):** H-link mooring shackle, 4 variants (MBL 45 t, 65 t, 85 t, 125 t). Chosen because mooring hardware is a recurring workspace-hub domain (#2070 cost-tracking, mooring-failures knowledge seed) and 4 variants exercises the "generate N from parameters" claim without inflating scope.

## Current State (document in the plan's Resource Intel section)

- Current `digitalmodel/` geometry pipeline — tools, inputs, outputs
- Where STEP files come from today (if at all)
- Which solver consumers exist and their geometry-input formats

## Go / No-Go Acceptance Criteria

All three must hold for **go**:

1. **Time-to-first-STEP < 30 min** for a Python-comfortable engineer working from CadQuery docs alone (no pre-existing exemplars)
2. **Regenerating all 4 H-link variants < 60 s** of compute total
3. **STEP → gmsh → AQWA `QPPL DIFF`** runs with no fatal mesh errors on first attempt for at least **2 of 4** variants

## Deliverable

- `digitalmodel/examples/cadquery-spike/h-link-family/` — 1 parametric script, 4 STEP outputs, 4 meshes, 1 successful AQWA run log
- `digitalmodel/examples/cadquery-spike/README.md` — timings, mesh quality notes, explicit verdict against the 3 criteria above

## Planning Workflow (per CLAUDE.md)

Plan file: `docs/plans/2026-MM-DD-issue-2327-cadquery-digitalmodel-spike.md` using `docs/plans/_template-issue-plan.md`. Resource-intel section must include the current-state documentation above. No implementation until `status:plan-approved`.

## References

- Wiki entity: `knowledge/wikis/engineering/wiki/entities/cadquery.md`
- Source summary: `knowledge/wikis/engineering/wiki/sources/2026-04-17-hn-cadquery.md`
- Marine cross-page: `knowledge/wikis/marine-engineering/wiki/entities/cadquery.md`
- Sibling issues: #2328 (tool comparison — covers the LLM-codegen question), #2329 (methodology decision — blocked by this)
- HN thread: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47772725

issues.title: epic: zero-loss agent learnings — git-track ALL AI agent memories, corrections, patterns, and insights
issues.body:
## Context

A full audit of all 4 AI agents (Claude Code, Hermes, Codex, Gemini) revealed that **~6.7GB of machine-local state** has NO git protection. If ace-linux-1 dies, the entire institutional memory built over months of agent interaction is lost.

The learnings that matter most — user corrections, learned patterns, permission rules, cross-agent insights — total only ~400KB but are scattered across 4 different home directories with no unified backup or portability strategy.

This is the umbrella issue coordinating the fix across all agents.

## Architecture: Three Tiers of Portability

### Tier 1: Git-committed snapshots (survives `git clone`)
Small, high-value files snapshotted nightly into workspace-hub repo:
- Agent memory files (Hermes MEMORY.md/USER.md, Claude project memory, Codex rules)
- Distilled learning artifacts (patterns, corrections, insights, drift summaries)
- Exported session metadata (JSONL tool-call summaries, not full transcripts)

### Tier 2: Rsync backup (survives single-machine failure)
Large files backed up to ace-linux-2 daily:
- Full session transcripts (Claude 2.5GB, Codex 899MB, Gemini 162MB, Hermes 124MB)
- SQLite databases (Hermes state.db 53MB, Codex state_5.sqlite 59MB)

### Tier 3: Regenerable (no backup needed)
Caches, plugins, debug logs, telemetry — recreated on agent install.

## Child Issues

| # | Issue | Agent | What's tracked | Size | Status |
|---|-------|-------|---------------|------|--------|
| #1777 | Hermes memory snapshots | Hermes | MEMORY.md, USER.md | 3KB | NEW |
| #1778 | Un-gitignore hermes/cross-agent state | Hermes/Cross | hermes-insights.yaml, cross-agent-memory.yaml, session JSONL | 15KB+11MB | NEW |
| #1779 | Claude project memory snapshots | Claude | 39 feedback/project/reference memory files | 196KB | NEW |
| #1780 | Fix nightly pipeline git-add gap | Claude/All | corrections/, patterns/, cc-insights/, reflect-history/, learned-patterns.json, etc. | ~25MB | NEW |
| #1781 | Codex + Gemini state snapshots | Codex/Gemini | default.rules, history.jsonl, state.json, session export | ~350KB | NEW |
| #1583 | Hermes config parity | Hermes | config.yaml template, SOUL.md | existing | OPEN |
| #894 | Knowledge persistence architecture | All | WRK completion learnings, career knowledge | existing | OPEN |
| #194 | Codex session archive integration | Codex | Session JSONL export pipeline | existing | OPEN |
| #193 | Session scanner for historical learnings | Claude | Retroactive learning extraction | existing | OPEN |

## Implementation Order

1. **#1780** (fix nightly pipeline) — Lowest effort, highest impact. Just add `git add` + commit for files already allowed by .gitignore exceptions. ~25MB of corrections, patterns, insights immediately saved.

2. **#1778** (un-gitignore hermes state) — Add 7 gitignore exceptions + commit existing files. Hermes insights, cross-agent memory, drift summary, portfolio signals.

3. **#1779** (Claude project memory) — Snapshot 39 memory files (196KB). Most valuable per-byte: every `feedback_*.md` is a user correction.

4. **#1777** (Hermes memory) — Snapshot MEMORY.md + USER.md (3KB).

5. **#1781** (Codex + Gemini) — Snapshot rules, state, history. Build Codex session export pipeline.

6. **#1583** (config parity) — Already scoped, extends to ace-linux-2.

## Nightly Pipeline Changes (consolidated)

All snapshot + commit logic should be consolidated into ONE script called at the end of `comprehensive-learning-nightly.sh`:

```bash
scripts/cron/commit-learning-artifacts.sh
```

This script:
1. Snapshots agent memories (Hermes, Claude, Codex, Gemini) to `config/agents/*/`
2. `git add` all learning state directories
3. Runs `legal-sanity-scan.sh --diff-only` (MANDATORY before commit)
4. Commits and pushes if anything changed

## Legal Risk

Memory files and correction records can contain file paths, command strings, or project names that reference client work. ALL snapshot directories must be covered by `legal-sanity-scan.sh`. The commit script must fail-safe: if legal scan finds violations, skip the commit and log the issue.

## What a Fresh `git clone` Gets You After This

```
config/agents/
  hermes/memories/          # Hermes MEMORY.md + USER.md snapshots
  claude/memory-snapshots/  # 39 Claude project memory files
  codex/state-snapshots/    # default.rules + history.jsonl
  gemini/state-snapshots/   # state.json + projects.json

.claude/state/
  corrections/              # Error correction history
  patterns/                 # Learned behavioral patterns
  reflect-history/          # Self-reflection analysis
  cc-insights/              # Agent insights
  learned-patterns.json     # Distilled pattern database
  cc-user-insights.yaml     # User preference model
  hermes-insights.yaml      # Cross-agent Hermes export
  cross-agent-memory.yaml   # Unified memory index
  drift-summary.yaml        # Config/skill drift tracking
  portfolio-signals.yaml    # Repo health signals
  skill-eval-results/       # Skill evaluation scores

logs/orchestrator/hermes/   # Hermes session exports (JSONL)
logs/orchestrator/codex/    # Codex session exports (JSONL, future)
```

Total: ~40MB of institutional memory that survives machine loss.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All child issues closed
- [ ] `git clone` on a fresh machine + `sync-agent-configs.sh` restores all agent memories
- [ ] Nightly pipeline commits all learning artifacts without manual intervention
- [ ] Legal scan gates all committed learning data
- [ ] Session transcript rsync backup covers all 4 agents
