## Context
A user requested extending llm-wiki completion from raw data to llm-wiki completeness for `/mnt/ace-data/raw data`.

Live prerequisite checks found:
- `/mnt/ace-data` resolves to `/mnt/ace`.
- The exact literal path `/mnt/ace-data/raw data` does **not** exist.
- Metadata-only discovery found 14 raw-like directories under `/mnt/ace-data` (`raw`, `raw_data`, or `Raw`), with no raw content copied into git/wiki.
- Existing overlap must be preserved: vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#13 is the llm-wiki roadmap anchor, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2392 is the coverage-gap detector issue, and vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2487 already delivered the raw-data-to-readiness spine/control-plane.

## Problem
The raw-like mounted source estate is not yet consistently classified into:
1. llm-wiki/document-intelligence candidates,
2. existing/in-flight coverage,
3. code/vendor/internal exclusions,
4. private/project-sensitive exclusions, and
5. future source-family package candidates requiring separate approval.

Without this metadata-only triage layer, agents risk either missing high-value source families or over-promoting raw/private/project data into git/wiki.

## Metadata-only inventory evidence
Representative discovered raw-like directories:

| Source path | Metadata-only count | Initial routing |
|---|---:|---|
| `/mnt/ace-data/O&G-Standards/raw` | 28,803 files / 692 dirs | standards candidate, reconcile with vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#25/#2373/#2392/#2487 and completed bounded standards promotions |
| `/mnt/ace-data/client_projects/energy_bsee/raw_data` | 10 files | offshore/BSEE candidate; no direct duplicate issue found |
| `/mnt/ace-data/digitalmodel/docs/aqwa/data/scripts/mooring_analysis/raw` | 28 files | AQWA candidate; map to vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2103 rather than duplicate |
| `/mnt/ace-data/digitalmodel/docs/orcaflex/literature/examples/raw` | 38 files / 76 dirs | OrcaFlex examples candidate; map to vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2124 rather than duplicate |
| `/mnt/ace-data/frontierdeepwater/data/raw` | 4 files / 1 dir | offshore source candidate; no direct duplicate issue found |
| `/mnt/ace-data/worldenergydata/data/modules/hse/raw` | 97 files / 7 dirs | HSE/safety data candidate; no direct duplicate issue found |
| `/mnt/ace-data/docs/disciplines/misc/projects/0136_das/.../Data/Raw` | 215 files / 8 dirs | indexed as `acma-projects`/project-management gap; project-sensitive until separately approved |

Non-corpus/exclusion examples include empty `.gitkeep` raw dirs, Rust crate internals, Struts image assets, QGIS generated DXF output, SSI marketing images, OPM parser source internals, and similar code/vendor/generated/personal/project-sensitive surfaces.

## Scope
Create a canonical plan for a metadata-only raw-like source triage and routing artifact. The plan should:
- preserve the raw-data boundary: no copying/promoting raw content to git/wiki;
- classify discovered raw-like roots by source family, sensitivity, target wiki/domain, existing issue mapping, and recommended next action;
- update or define a durable metadata/routing artifact under the document-intelligence surface;
- link resulting source-family work back to vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#13, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2392, and vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2487;
- identify which families need separate follow-up issues before any summary promotion.

## Out of scope
- No raw data import into git/wiki.
- No direct llm-wiki page generation from raw documents in this issue.
- No standards content extraction from proprietary/copyrighted documents.
- No project-sensitive corpus promotion (SESA/Woodfibre/ACMA/DAS/client material) without separate explicit approval.
- No implementation before canonical plan review and user approval.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A canonical plan is created under `docs/plans/` and indexed in `docs/plans/README.md`.
- [ ] The plan cites the metadata-only inventory, `data/document-index/mounted-source-registry.yaml`, `data/document-index/index.jsonl`, `docs/document-intelligence/data-intelligence-map.md`, vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#13, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2392, and vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2487.
- [ ] The plan includes a raw-like source routing matrix covering all discovered raw-like roots.
- [ ] Existing/in-flight issue mappings are explicit: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2103 for AQWA, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2124 for OrcaFlex examples, vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#25/#2373/standards wave issues for O&G standards, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2540/#2541-#2544/#2559 for Elements-derived material.
- [ ] The final plan-review comment requests user approval and labels this issue `status:plan-review`.

{"content": "# Issue Planning Workflow — Onboarding Guide and Plan Index

This document is the single onboarding reference for the mandatory issue planning workflow.
All agents (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Hermes) must follow this workflow for every GitHub issue.

## Why Planning Is Mandatory

Historical data shows that agents skipping the planning step produced incorrect implementations, wasted tokens, and created rework. The planning workflow catches problems before implementation begins, when they are cheapest to fix.

- **Plan review** answers: "Is this the right thing to build?"
- **Cross-review** answers: "Was the right thing built correctly?"

Both are required. Neither replaces the other.

## The Workflow (Step by Step)

```
1. INTAKE           — Read issue, classify complexity (T1/T2/T3)
2. RESOURCE INTEL   — Search existing code, standards, documents, prior plans
3. DRAFT PLAN       — Copy template, fill all sections, save to docs/plans/
4. ADVERSARIAL REVIEW — Route to 2+ AI providers; revise if MAJOR verdict
5. POST TO GITHUB   — Comment plan on issue, label status:plan-review
6. HARD STOP        — Wait for user approval (never self-approve)
7. USER APPROVES    — Swap label to status:plan-approved
8. IMPLEMENT        — TDD: tests first, then code, then full suite
9. CLOSE            — Commit, push, post summary, close issue
```

### Step 1: Intake

- Read the full issue body — scope, acceptance criteria, references
- Classify complexity:
  - **T1** (trivial): config, typo, single-file fix — brief plan, still requires approval
  - **T2** (standard): new module, multiple files, tests — full workflow
  - **T3** (complex): multi-module, architecture, standards — full workflow + subagents

### Step 2: Resource Intelligence

Before writing anything, search all available sources. The retrieval contract (#2208) defines minimum requirements by issue class.

**Universal minimum (ALL issues):**
- **Prior plans**: `docs/plans/` directory and this index
- **Existing code**: search relevant repos in affected paths for prior implementations
- **Recent issues**: related open/closed issues that may overlap or conflict
- **Intelligence entry points**: `docs/document-intelligence/README.md` (when available per #2104) or `docs/document-intelligence/data-intelligence-map.md`

**Issue-class-specific additions:**

| Issue class | Labels / triggers | Additional required sources |
|---|---|---|
| **General** | Default (no specific class match) | Universal minimum is sufficient |
| **Engineering** | `cat:engineering`, `cat:engineering-calculations`, `cat:engineering-methodology` | `standards-transfer-ledger.yaml`, `code-registry.yaml`, relevant domain wiki under `knowledge/wikis/`, `online-resource-registry.yaml` |
| **Data Pipeline** | `cat:data-pipeline` | `registry.yaml`, pipeline config, `resource-intelligence-maturity.yaml` |
| **Documentation** | `cat:documentation` | Governance docs in target directory, `CONTROL_PLANE_CONTRACT.md`, durable-vs-transient boundary policy (#2209) |
| **Harness/Infra** | `cat:harness` | `CONTROL_PLANE_CONTRACT.md`, `config/agents/` settings, `.claude/rules/` |
| **Knowledge/Intelligence** | Issues under #2205 tree, or touching `knowledge/`, `docs/document-intelligence/` | Operating model (#2205), sibling contracts (#2207, #2209), accessibility map (#2096), accessibility registry (when available per #2136) |

If classification is ambiguous or unlabeled, default to **General**. If an issue matches multiple classes, consult the **union** of all matching bundles.

**Evidence requirements:**
- ≥3 distinct sources must be listed in the plan's Resource Intelligence Summary (issue body counts as 1)
- Each source must cite a specific file path, issue number, or registry entry
- Each source must state a concrete finding — not vague claims like "searched the repo"
- The Gaps sub-section must list what must be built from scratch

Full retrieval contract specification: `docs/plans/2026-04-11-issue-2208-intelligence-retrieval-contract-for-github-issue-workflows.md`

### Step 3: Draft Plan

1. Copy the template: `docs/plans/_template-issue-plan.md`
2. Save as: `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-issue-NNN-slug.md`
3. Fill all required sections (see "Required Sections" below)
4. Add a row to the Index table in this file

### Step 4: Adversarial Review

Route the plan to at least 2 other AI providers. Each gives a verdict:
- **APPROVE** — plan is sound
- **MINOR** — small issues, can proceed after fixing
- **MAJOR** — significant issues, must revise and re-review

Save review artifacts to `scripts/review/results/YYYY-MM-DD-plan-NNN-<agent>.md`.

#### Canonical way to run the adversarial wave (#2323)

```bash
scripts/review/plan-review-fanout.sh docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-issue-NNN-slug.md
```

This wraps Claude + Codex + Gemini in parallel under the shared stance contract
at `scripts/review/plan-review-prompt.md`. It writes one per-provider artifact
plus a `-disagreement.md` summarizing verdict splits + per-provider unique
findings. Per-provider invocation shape is tuned to each CLI's known quirks
(Codex and Gemini get INLINE plan body; Claude gets an `@`-path reference;
Gemini runs from `cwd=/tmp` to dodge the `.gemini/agents/*.md` permissionMode
validation bug). Single-provider failure does not abort the other two — the
failing provider's artifact records `UNAVAILABLE`.

Flags:

- `--providers=claude,codex,gemini` — subset of providers (comma-separated).
- `--output-dir=<dir>` — override the default `scripts/review/results/` sink
  (useful for batch / worktree / test runs).

### Step 5: Post and Label

1. Post the completed plan as a GitHub issue comment
2. Apply label: `gh issue edit NNN --add-label "status:plan-review"`
3. **STOP** — do NOT write any implementation code

### Step 6: User Approval

The user (never the implementing agent) approves the plan:
- `gh issue edit NNN --remove-label "status:plan-review" --add-label "status:plan-approved"`
- Creates marker: `.planning/plan-approved/NNN.md`

### Step 7: Implement (TDD)

Only after `status:plan-approved` label exists:
1. Write tests first — confirm they fail
2. Implement minimum code to pass tests
3. Run full test suite — confirm no regressions
4. Self-review against approved plan

### Step 8: Close

- Conventional commit referencing the issue number
- Push to remote
- Post summary comment on issue: what was done, test results, review verdicts
- Close the issue

**Retrieval evidence at closeout** (per #2208 contract):
- The close comment must include a "Sources consumed" line listing intelligence assets that materially informed implementation (≥1 item)
- The close comment should include a "Promotion candidates" line: "none" or specific findings worth promoting from transient (L5) to durable knowledge (L3) per #2209 Section 7

### Retrieval Evidence at Review Time

Adversarial review artifacts (`scripts/review/results/YYYY-MM-DD-plan-NNN-<agent>.md`) should include a Retrieval Adequacy assessment:

| Check | What the reviewer verifies |
|---|---|
| Resource Intelligence Summary non-empty, ≥3 sources | Plan contains adequate evidence |
| Issue-class-specific sources checked | Obvious sources for the issue class were not missed |
| Evidence is specific | Plan cites file paths and concrete findings, not vague claims |

Reviewers should note a retrieval verdict: `adequate` or `insufficient` with specific gaps.

## Batch / Overnight Sessions

When the user is not present:
- Draft plans and label `status:plan-review` — do NOT implement
- Only implement issues already labeled `status:plan-approved`
- User reviews results the next morning

## Status Meanings

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| draft | Plan file exists locally but has not yet completed adversarial review |
| adversarial-reviewed | Frontier-model review passed; ready to post for user review |
| plan-review | Posted to GitHub; waiting for user approval |
| plan-approved | User approved; ready for implementation or batch execution |
| superseded | Replaced by a newer version of the plan |
| completed | Issue implemented and closed |

## Required Sections in Each Plan

Every plan file must include (see `_template-issue-plan.md` for full format):

1. **Resource Intelligence Summary** — evidence contract: ≥3 sources with specific paths/findings, issue-class-appropriate sources, gaps identified (see template and #2208 contract)
2. **Artifact Map** — paths to plan, tests, implementation, review files
3. **Deliverable** — one sentence: what will exist after this issue is done
4. **Pseudocode** — 5-15 lines per function (T2/T3); "trivial" note for T1
5. **Files to Change** — action, path, reason for each file
6. **TDD Test List** — one row per test with name, verification, input, output
7. **Acceptance Criteria** — checkboxes for all verification steps
8. **Adversarial Review Summary** — provider, verdict, key findings
9. **Risks and Open Questions** — what could go wrong, what needs user input
10. **Complexity** — T1, T2, or T3 with justification

## Enforcement

- **PreToolUse hook**: `.claude/hooks/plan-approval-gate.sh` blocks writes without approval marker
- **Pre-commit hook**: `scripts/enforcement/require-plan-approval.sh --strict` blocks commits without approval
- **Labels**: `status:plan-review` (orange) and `status:plan-approved` (green) exist on the repo

{"content": "# Design: anthropics/financial-services → llm-wiki engineering/ ingest

- **Date:** 2026-05-09
- **Target repo:** `vamseeachanta/llm-wiki` (nested at `/mnt/local-analysis/workspace-hub/llm-wiki/`)
- **Source URL:** https://github.com/anthropics/financial-services
- **Source license:** Apache-2.0 (permissive — synthesis allowed; no verbatim README dumps)
- **Source pushed_at observed:** 2026-05-07T21:10:05Z
- **Workflow:** 8-step external-post ingest (`memory/project_llm_wiki_external_post_ingest_workflow.md`)
- **Deviation from default workflow:** source is a GitHub repo, not a LinkedIn/blog post. Steps 1 (WebFetch) and 5 (concept page) bend; everything else holds.

## Why this lands here

Anthropic's "Claude for Financial Services" is a marketplace of agent plugins and Managed Agent cookbooks (Pitch Agent, GL Reconciler, KYC Screener, etc.) for finance verticals (IB, equity research, PE, wealth management). The financial-domain content has no consumer in `llm-wiki` today — its 8 domain wikis are offshore/marine.

What is consumable: the **multi-agent architecture patterns** the repo demonstrates concretely — managed-agent cookbooks (`agent.yaml` + leaf-worker subagents + `steering-examples.json`), the `callable_agents` research-preview pattern, `handoff_request` events as the cross-agent control plane, and the dual-deployment principle (one source tree → Cowork plugin **and** Managed Agent template share the same skills). These map directly to existing `engineering/wiki/` meta-AI material:

- Existing peer sources: `agent-equivalence-architecture-doc.md`, `ai-agent-guidelines-doc.md`, `ai-development-ecosystem-doc.md`, `compound-engineering-methodology.md`, `methodology-docs.md`
- Existing peer concepts: `agent-delegation`, `orchestrator-worker-separation`, `multi-agent-parity`, `compound-engineering`

So this lands as a **source page** in `engineering/wiki/sources/`, ignoring the financial-services domain content and capturing only the agent-architecture lessons.

## Out of scope

- No new concept page (`managed-agent-orchestration.md`) — gap acknowledged but deferred per YAGNI; promote later if downstream code/chatbots surface the need.
- No touches to other domain wikis (`asset-management/`, etc.) — the org-name "asset management" overlap is coincidental; that wiki is physical-asset-focused.
- No vendor-PDF archival — none involved.
- No issue filed against `vamseeachanta/llm-wiki` — single-page additions don't require issue tracking under the current workflow.

Path: `llm-wiki/wikis/engineering/wiki/sources/anthropics-2026-financial-services-managed-agents.md`

Author = `anthropics` (org-as-author, since no individual maintainer is canonical for the repo); year = 2026 (repo activity confirms 2026 timeframe); topic-slug = `financial-services-managed-agents` (captures both the repo identity and the agent-architecture angle).

title: "Claude for Financial Services — managed-agent reference patterns"
tags: [managed-agents, multi-agent-orchestration, plugin-architecture, anthropic, agent-handoff, leaf-worker-subagents]
added: 2026-05-09

sources:

- **Relevance** — why an Anthropic finance-vertical reference repo is methodology-grade input for a marine/offshore wiki: the agent architecture is domain-agnostic; finance is incidental to what's being captured.
- **Key teachings** — bullet list:
  - Managed-agent cookbook structure: `agent.yaml` + `subagents/*.yaml` (leaf workers, depth-1) + `steering-examples.json`.
  - `callable_agents` research-preview pattern: orchestrator delegates to depth-1 leaf workers, not arbitrary depth recursion.
  - `handoff_request` steering events as the cross-agent control plane, with a reference event loop in `scripts/orchestrate.py`.
  - Dual-surface principle: one source tree compiles to both a Cowork plugin (`plugins/agent-plugins/<slug>/`) and a Managed Agent template (`managed-agent-cookbooks/<slug>/`), sharing identical system prompts and skills.
  - Self-contained agent plugins bundle synced copies of vertical-plugin skills — install one plugin, get everything that agent needs.
  - Vertical plugins decouple skills+commands+connectors from end-to-end agents, so a user can install `/comps` without installing Pitch Agent.
  - Partner-built plugins (`plugins/partner-built/lseg`, `plugins/partner-built/spglobal`) demonstrate the ecosystem extension pattern.

  - `concepts/agent-delegation.md` — base pattern; this source adds `callable_agents` as the API-surface name and the depth-1 constraint.
  - `concepts/orchestrator-worker-separation.md` — repo's `agent.yaml` (orchestrator) + `subagents/*.yaml` (workers) is a concrete instantiation.
  - `concepts/multi-agent-parity.md` — the dual-surface principle is parity through shared source.
  - `sources/agent-equivalence-architecture-doc.md` — closest peer source; this entry extends it with managed-agent specifics.
- **Use as a wiki source** — citation pointer for future managed-agent or plugin-architecture wiki content. (The `concepts/managed-agent-orchestration.md` gap is tracked in this governance doc's "Deferred follow-ups" section, not in the published wiki page.)

issue.body:
## Context
Parent: #2507
Roadmap: `docs/roadmaps/chip-design-cad-fem-career-roadmap.md`

Build a Python-first geometry/layout automation example that bridges CAD practices into semiconductor layout and package/interposer-style structures.

## Proposed scope
- Use KLayout scripting and/or GDSFactory to generate a parameterized layout artifact.
- Export/import GDS/OASIS and at least one human-inspectable representation such as SVG/DXF where practical.
- Extract metadata: layers, polygons, bounding boxes, ports/nets where available, geometry invariants.
- Include tests around geometry invariants and repeatability.

## Deliverables
1. Python module/script for parameterized layout generation.
2. Sample output artifacts or reproducible generation command.
3. Metadata extraction report.
4. Tests and documentation.

## Acceptance criteria
- Demo can be run locally without proprietary tools.
- Generated artifacts are deterministic enough for tests or snapshot checks.
- Report explains relevance to chip design, packaging, and CAD automation roles.

Integrate the naval-architecture-focused codes now copied to `/mnt/ace/acma-codes` into the workspace-hub intelligence ecosystem so they become discoverable, reusable, and promotable into llm-wikis and related repo workflows.

## Why
A new code/source collection is now available at `/mnt/ace/acma-codes`. If it remains only as a filesystem drop, the ecosystem loses most of its value:
- it will not be discoverable through resource/document intelligence
- it will not participate in provenance-aware promotion into llm-wikis
- future issues will not benefit from it during planning/execution/review
- cross-machine access and canonical-location policy will remain undefined

This needs to be integrated into the same emerging operating model being defined in vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2205 and related child issues.

- inventory the contents of `/mnt/ace/acma-codes`
- classify what the collection contains:
  - raw standards/codes
  - notes/summaries
  - translated/promoted artifacts
  - mixed-source duplicates
- determine how the collection should enter the repo ecosystem:
  - resource intelligence
  - document intelligence / registry / ledger coverage
  - llm-wiki promotion path
  - canonical entry points and accessibility surfaces
- define provenance expectations so these codes do not become an untracked parallel source of truth
- identify what should be promoted directly into llm-wikis versus what should remain in registry/provenance layers
- identify cross-machine accessibility assumptions and any mount/path dependencies
- create follow-on implementation tasks if ingestion, indexing, deduplication, or wiki promotion must be split

Each AI agent in the ecosystem (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Hermes orchestrator) currently re-implements doc-intelligence access patterns:
- Claude Code: grep + `Read` + skill recall.
- Codex: limited — no filesystem access from sandbox (per `feedback_codex_needs_pushed_artifact.md`).
- Gemini: inconsistent; no unified lookup.
- Hermes: custom Python helpers in `scripts/orchestrator/hermes/`.

This causes:
1. Duplicated retrieval code across agents.
2. Codex cannot participate in retrieval-gated workflows (#2208) because it can't read `data/document-index/`.
3. No single point to measure retrieval quality or log queries.
4. #1804 is evaluating external MCP servers but nothing builds an *internal* MCP server for our own intelligence.

## Deliverable

An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server exposing read-only tools for the doc-intelligence ecosystem:

| Tool | Inputs | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `doc_key_lookup` | `doc_key` | registry entry, paths, provenance, status |
| `wiki_search` | query string, domain filter | top-K L3 page paths + excerpts |
| `registry_query` | YAML path filter, field filter | matching registry rows |
| `coverage_status` | discipline/domain | wiki-coverage metrics for that domain |
| `cfr_lookup` | Title, part/section | CFR registry entry + text (depends on CFR-ingestion issue) |

Transport: stdio MCP per standard; optional HTTP bridge for Hermes.
Location: `scripts/mcp/doc_intel_server/` (Python using `mcp` SDK).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] MCP server at `scripts/mcp/doc_intel_server/server.py` with `pyproject.toml` declaring it
- [ ] All 5 tools implemented with JSON-schema input validation
- [ ] Registered in Claude Code `.claude/mcp-servers/doc-intel.json`
- [ ] Registered in Gemini CLI config (`.gemini/mcp-servers.yaml` or equivalent)
- [ ] Hermes orchestrator can invoke via stdio or HTTP-bridge
- [ ] Rate-limited query logging to `logs/mcp/doc-intel/queries-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` for audit
- [ ] Test suite covers: tool schema validation, empty result handling, concurrent access
- [ ] Documentation at `docs/document-intelligence/mcp-server.md` (usage, tool reference, examples)
- [ ] No writes — server is read-only (enforced at tool level, tested)

## Dependencies

- Hard-depends on: embeddings-index issue (this bundle) — backs `wiki_search`
- Soft-depends on: retrieval-augmented-planner issue (this bundle) — shares the embeddings corpus
- Soft-depends on: CFR-ingestion issue (this bundle) — backs `cfr_lookup` (can be stub on first ship)
- Relates to: #1804 (MCP server evaluation) — this is the first internal MCP server and should inform the evaluation framework

## Notes

- Read-only by design: no promotion, no writes, no mutations. Write paths remain in existing scripts.
- Codex impact: per `feedback_codex_needs_pushed_artifact.md`, Codex sandbox blocks filesystem reads. The MCP server bridges this — Codex can invoke MCP tools to retrieve doc-intel without local FS access.
- Performance budget: <500ms p95 for `doc_key_lookup`; <2s p95 for `wiki_search` with embeddings backend.
- Security: server must not expose `.env`, `config/secrets/`, or any gitignored path; path allowlist enforced at tool layer.

{"issue": {"url": "https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2393", "title": "feat(doc-intel): embeddings index over L2 registry + L3 wiki pages (nightly refresh)", "issue_number": 2393, "body": "## Problem

All retrieval across L2 (registry) and L3 (LLM-wikis) today is substring-based (grep, ripgrep, path lookup). This blocks:
- "Find prior work similar to this issue" queries for the retrieval-augmented planner (parallel issue in this bundle).
- Semantic-similarity checks when promoting handoffs (#2374), WRK completions (#2375), and analysis reports.
- Cross-wiki link discovery beyond what vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#36/#2068 produce via explicit anchors.

vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#1772 closed a semantic-search index for 6 standards orgs (525 files) but was not generalized to the unified L2+L3 corpus.

## Deliverable

A nightly-refreshed embeddings index keyed by `doc_key` (per operating model §3) covering:
- All L2 registry entries with non-null summary or extracted content.
- All L3 wiki pages (`knowledge/wikis/*/wiki/**/*.md`) with content-addressable chunk IDs.

Storage: `data/document-index/embeddings.parquet` (or `.duckdb`) + `data/document-index/embeddings-manifest.yaml` (model name, version, refresh timestamp, row counts).

Query CLI: `uv run python scripts/knowledge/query_embeddings.py --text "..." --top-k 10 --layer L2|L3|both`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Index build script `scripts/knowledge/build_embeddings_index.py` runs end-to-end on current corpus
- [ ] Query CLI returns top-K `doc_key`s with similarity scores and source paths
- [ ] Row-count + refresh-timestamp committed to `embeddings-manifest.yaml` (git-tracked; Parquet file gitignored if >10 MB, cached at `/mnt/ace/`)
- [ ] Nightly refresh wired into `config/scheduled-tasks/schedule-tasks.yaml`
- [ ] Model selection documented in `docs/document-intelligence/embeddings-model-selection.md` (spike deliverable; BGE-M3 / Voyage / `text-embedding-3-large` comparison)
- [ ] Unit tests cover: index build idempotency, query result stability, model-version gating
- [ ] Conforms to operating model §7 cross-machine tier rules: manifest is git-tracked; Parquet may live on shared mount

## Dependencies

- Depends on: vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#23 (`doc_key` in wiki frontmatter), vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2361 (merged_at rename), vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2362 (ledger doc_key backfill) — all must be `plan-approved` before index build is reliable
- Relates to: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2363 (wiki_refs reverse lookup — embeddings and reverse-lookup are complementary retrieval paths)
- Blocks: retrieval-augmented-planner issue (this bundle), doc-intel MCP server issue (this bundle)

## Notes

- Model selection is a separable sub-deliverable; plan should include an explicit spike for this.
- Cost envelope: for current corpus (~50k docs) re-embedding weekly at ~$0.02/M tokens with `text-embedding-3-large` is <$5/week. Local BGE-M3 via Ollama is $0 compute, higher latency. Plan should pick with evidence.

{"issue": {"url": "https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2655", "title": "chore(provider-session): route Codex nested-repo path drift to owning tier-1 repos", "issue_number": 2655, "body": "## Summary

Plan a bounded remediation for Codex provider-session `nested_repo_context_drift`: Codex logs are still reading tier-1 sibling/nested repository paths as if they were missing `workspace-hub` files. The next stream should make this routing explicit in provider-session prompts/docs/tests so Codex re-resolves the owning repo root before treating those reads as workspace-hub stale-path debt.

## Evidence

Latest provider-session audit (`analysis/provider-session-ecosystem-audit.json`, generated `2026-05-07T09:37:54Z`) reports for Codex:

- `missing_repo_reads`: `730`
- remediation hint `nested_repo_context_drift`: `61`
- top matched examples:
  - `src/worldenergydata/cost/data_collection/calibration_schema.py` — 9
  - `src/worldenergydata/cost/data_collection/public_dataset.py` — 8
  - `src/worldenergydata/cost/data_collection/__init__.py` — 8
  - `docs/plans/2026-04-21-issue-334-annual-operator-disclosures-dataset.md` — 8
  - `src/assethold/signals/watchlist.py` — 7
  - `sitemap.xml` — 7
  - `src/worldenergydata/cost/calibration/cost_predictor.py` — 7
  - `tests/unit/cost/test_proxy_comparison.py` — 7

Canonical guidance already exists in `docs/ops/legacy-claude-reference-map.md` under “Session-local worktree and nested repo path drift”: examples map `src/worldenergydata/*` → `worldenergydata/src/worldenergydata/*`, `tests/unit/cost/*` → `worldenergydata/tests/unit/cost/*`, `src/assethold/*` → `assethold/src/assethold/*`, and `sitemap.xml` → `aceengineer-website/sitemap.xml`.

## Scope

Planning only until approved:

- Add an approval-gated plan artifact under `docs/plans/`.
- Define Codex-facing routing/remediation requirements for nested tier-1 repo paths.
- Require tests or fixtures proving nested repo path examples are classified/routed without being recreated in `workspace-hub`.
- Link this issue to the provider-session audit and prior classification work (#2333) without duplicating already-closed non-repo-artifact classification work.

## Out of scope

- Recreating any missing `src/worldenergydata/*`, `src/assethold/*`, or website files under `workspace-hub`.
- Changing sibling repositories before this plan is reviewed and approved.
- LLM-wiki spinout cleanup; that is already covered by #2650 unless a narrower approved sub-plan is later required.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Canonical issue plan exists in `docs/plans/` and cites audit evidence, related issues, and redirect guidance.
- [ ] Plan includes TDD fixtures for Codex nested repo path routing.

## Summary

Plan a bounded remediation for Codex provider-session `nested_repo_context_drift`: Codex logs are still reading tier-1 sibling/nested repository paths as if they were missing `workspace-hub` files. The next stream should make this routing explicit in provider-session prompts/docs/tests so Codex re-resolves the owning repo root before treating those reads as workspace-hub stale-path debt.

## Evidence

Latest provider-session audit (`analysis/provider-session-ecosystem-audit.json`, generated `2026-05-07T09:37:54Z`) reports for Codex:

- `missing_repo_reads`: `730`
- remediation hint `nested_repo_context_drift`: `61`
- top matched examples:
  - `src/worldenergydata/cost/data_collection/calibration_schema.py` — 9
  - `src/worldenergydata/cost/data_collection/public_dataset.py` — 8
  - `src/worldenergydata/cost/data_collection/__init__.py` — 8
  - `docs/plans/2026-04-21-issue-334-annual-operator-disclosures-dataset.md` — 8
  - `src/assethold/signals/watchlist.py` — 7
  - `sitemap.xml` — 7
  - `src/worldenergydata/cost/calibration/cost_predictor.py` — 7
  - `tests/unit/cost/test_proxy_comparison.py` — 7

Canonical guidance already exists in `docs/ops/legacy-claude-reference-map.md` under “Session-local worktree and nested repo path drift”: examples map `src/worldenergydata/*` → `worldenergydata/src/worldenergydata/*`, `tests/unit/cost/*` → `worldenergydata/tests/unit/cost/*`, `src/assethold/*` → `assethold/src/assethold/*`, and `sitemap.xml` → `aceengineer-website/sitemap.xml`.

## Scope

Planning only until approved:

- Add an approval-gated plan artifact under `docs/plans/`.
- Define Codex-facing routing/remediation requirements for nested tier-1 repo paths.
- Require tests or fixtures proving nested repo path examples are classified/routed without being recreated in `workspace-hub`.
- Link this issue to the provider-session audit and prior classification work (#2333) without duplicating already-closed non-repo-artifact classification work.

## Out of scope

- Recreating any missing `src/worldenergydata/*`, `src/assethold/*`, or website files under `workspace-hub`.
- Changing sibling repositories before this plan is reviewed and approved.
- LLM-wiki spinout cleanup; that is already covered by #2650 unless a narrower approved sub-plan is later required.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Canonical issue plan exists in `docs/plans/` and cites audit evidence, related issues, and redirect guidance.
- [ ] Plan includes TDD fixtures for Codex nested repo path routing.
- [ ] Plan distinguishes actionable workspace-hub stale-path debt from sibling repo routing drift.
- [ ] Plan receives review and is moved to `status:plan-review` for user approval.

- [ ] issue serves as the coordination surface for broad LLM-wiki strengthening rather than duplicating implementation scope

{"issue": {"url": "https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2128", "title": "fix(governance): wire enforcement-env and require-review-on-push into install-hooks pre-push chain", "issue_number": 2128, "body": "## Problem
`install-hooks.sh` claims to install a strict pre-push governance chain, but the generated pre-push hook omits key pieces.

Evidence from live review:
- `scripts/enforcement/install-hooks.sh` says pre-push should chain:
  `review-gate -> stage-prompt-drift-gate -> repo/test gates`
- The generated `.git/hooks/pre-push` currently only contains the stage-prompt-drift block
- It does **not** source `.git/hooks/enforcement-env`
- It does **not** call `scripts/enforcement/require-review-on-push.sh`
- In a clean temp repo, adding `DISABLE_ENFORCEMENT=1` to `.git/hooks/enforcement-env` had no effect because pre-push never sourced it

## Why this matters

Establish the repo-tracked portability contract for core engineering work so durable OpenFOAM/Blender learnings do not remain machine-local.

Part of #1782.
Related: #26, #25, #1268, #1475.

## Motivation
The ecosystem needs a canonical policy layer that defines:
- what counts as portable engineering knowledge
- what must be captured in repos vs what may remain machine-local
- machine role boundaries between orchestration and execution hosts
- a completion checklist for reusable engineering work

## Scope
Create Phase 1 documentation only. No OpenFOAM or Blender implementation changes in this issue.

Proposed docs:
- `docs/engineering/portability/PORTABILITY_CONTRACT.md`
- `docs/engineering/portability/MACHINE_ROLES.md`
- `docs/engineering/portability/ENGINEERING_DELIVERY_CHECKLIST.md`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `PORTABILITY_CONTRACT.md` defines portable vs machine-local engineering knowledge
- [ ] `MACHINE_ROLES.md` defines dev-primary vs dev-secondary responsibilities
- [ ] `ENGINEERING_DELIVERY_CHECKLIST.md` defines the minimum reusable artifact bundle
- [ ] docs explicitly state that durable learnings must be promoted into repo-tracked artifacts
- [ ] docs cross-reference current workstation registry and relevant downstream engineering issues

## Notes
Recommended defaults to encode:
- dev-primary = orchestration/control/documentation host
- dev-secondary = canonical engineering execution host

issue.body:
## Summary
Establish the repo-tracked portability contract for core engineering work so durable OpenFOAM/Blender learnings do not remain machine-local.

Part of #1782.
Related: #26, #25, #1268, #1475.

## Motivation
The ecosystem needs a canonical policy layer that defines:
- what counts as portable engineering knowledge
- what must be captured in repos vs what may remain machine-local
- machine role boundaries between orchestration and execution hosts
- a completion checklist for reusable engineering work

## Scope
Create Phase 1 documentation only. No OpenFOAM or Blender implementation changes in this issue.

Proposed docs:
- `docs/engineering/portability/PORTABILITY_CONTRACT.md`
- `docs/engineering/portability/MACHINE_ROLES.md`
- `docs/engineering/portability/ENGINEERING_DELIVERY_CHECKLIST.md`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `PORTABILITY_CONTRACT.md` defines portable vs machine-local engineering knowledge
- [ ] `MACHINE_ROLES.md` defines dev-primary vs dev-secondary responsibilities
- [ ] `ENGINEERING_DELIVERY_CHECKLIST.md` defines the minimum reusable artifact bundle
- [ ] docs explicitly state that durable learnings must be promoted into repo-tracked artifacts
- [ ] docs cross-reference current workstation registry and relevant downstream engineering issues

## Notes
Recommended defaults to encode:
- dev-primary = orchestration/control/documentation host
- dev-secondary = canonical engineering execution host
- OpenFOAM baseline = ESI/OpenFOAM.com v2312 (for downstream phases)
- Blender baseline = headless `blender -b --python ...` (for downstream phases)

# Swarm 3 - Plan-Review Drift Audit

Date: 2026-05-10
Scope: governance/audit-only. No labels, issues, source code, tests, or approval markers were changed.

## Executive summary

This audit inspected the current `status:plan-review`, `status:plan-approved`, `status:blocked`, and active execution-adjacent issue state through GitHub issue metadata/comments and committed planning artifacts on `main`.

Key result: #2269 and #2402 are unsafe execution candidates. Both retain `status:plan-approved` while also carrying `status:blocked`, and both have issue-comment evidence saying execution must not resume until external blockers are resolved.

The plan-review queue also contains historical closed issues that still retain `status:plan-review`. These are label hygiene defects, not live execution candidates. Some open plan-review items are intentionally not approval-ready because they need rereview or a durable plan artifact.

Local shell access failed during this run with `bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted`, so local inspection used committed GitHub files where available: `docs/plans/README.md`, plan artifacts linked from comments, approval markers on `main`, and issue comments.
